# f5xc_http_loadbalancer (Resource)

HTTP Load Balancer view defines a required parameters that can be used in CRUD, to create and manage HTTP Load Balancer.<br>It can be used to create HTTP Load Balancer and HTTPS Load Balancer.<br><br>View will create following child objects.<br><br>* virtual_host<br>* routes<br>* clusters<br>* endpoints<br>* advertise_policy

To get more information about f5xc_http_loadbalancer, refer:

- [API documentation](https://docs.cloud.f5.com/docs-v2/api/views-http-loadbalancer)

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Example: Http Loadbalancer - Full

resource "f5xc_origin_pool" "example" {
  name                   = "example-http-op-n602nzk4"
  namespace              = "default"
  description            = "Acceptance test origin pool for HTTP load balancer"
  loadbalancer_algorithm = ["ROUND_ROBIN"]
  endpoint_selection     = ["LOCAL_PREFERRED"]

  port_choice = {
    port = 8080
  }

  origin_servers = [
    {
      choice = {
        public_name = {
          dns_name = "example.com"
        }
      }
    }
  ]

  tls_choice = {
    no_tls = true
  }

  upstream_conn_pool_reuse_type = {
    map_downstream_to_upstream_conn_pool_type_choice = {
      disable_conn_pool_reuse = true
    }
  }
}

resource "f5xc_http_loadbalancer" "example" {
  name      = "example-http-lb-n602nzk4"
  namespace = "default"

  description = "Acceptance test HTTP load balancer updated"
  labels = { env = "staging", tier = "edge" }

  domains = ["example-http-lb-n602nzk4.example.com"]

  loadbalancer_type_choice = {
    http = {
      port_choice = {
        port = 8880
      }
    }
  }

  advertise_choice = {
    advertise_on_public_default_vip = true
  }

  default_route_pools = [
    {
      pool_choice = {
        pool = {
          name      = f5xc_origin_pool.example.name
          namespace = f5xc_origin_pool.example.namespace
        }
      }
      weight   = 1
      priority = 1
    }
  ]

  waf_choice = {
    disable_waf = true
  }

  challenge_type_choice = {
    js_challenge = {
      js_script_delay = 2000
    }
  }

  user_id_choice = {
    user_id_client_ip = true
  }

  rate_limit_choice = {
    disable_rate_limit = true
  }

  service_policy_choice = {
    service_policies_from_namespace = true
  }

  hash_policy_choice = {
    least_active = true
  }

  trust_client_ip_headers_choice = {
    disable_trust_client_ip_headers = true
  }

  malicious_user_detection_choice = {
    disable_malicious_user_detection = true
  }

  api_discovery_choice = {
    disable_api_discovery = true
  }

  bot_defense_choice = {
    disable_bot_defense = true
  }

  api_definition_choice = {
    disable_api_definition = true
  }

  sensitive_data_policy_choice = {
    default_sensitive_data_policy = true
  }

  api_testing_choice = {
    disable_api_testing = true
  }

  threat_mesh_choice = {
    disable_threat_mesh = true
  }

  malware_protection_choice = {
    disable_malware_protection = true
  }

  
  
  
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `api_discovery_choice` (Attributes) API Discovery Choice When enabled, sampled traffic passing through this load balancer is analyzed and APIs exposed by the application are identified. An API is identified by its canonical (collapsed) URL path and the method used to call it. Once all APIs are identified, for each API, the system learns its possible schema. The learnt schema for all APIs is used to automatically generate a swagger definition file for the entire API set exposed by this load balancer. The feature can be configured also via external app_type and labeling this HTTP Load Balancer. In this case external app_type configuration overrides internally disabled feature. Enabling the feature internally is allowed only when no labeling to external app_type.<br>Exactly one of `disable_api_discovery` or `enable_api_discovery` must be specified. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_discovery_choice))
- `api_testing_choice` (Attributes) Api testing Enable or disable security testing for API endpoints to ensure a secure development pipeline.<br>Exactly one of `api_testing` or `disable_api_testing` must be specified. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_testing_choice))
- `domains` (List of String) Domains A list of Domains (host/authority header) that will be matched to load balancer. Supported Domains and search order: 1. Exact Domain names: www.foo.com. 2. Domains starting with a Wildcard: *.foo.com. Not supported Domains: - Just a Wildcard: * - A Wildcard and TLD with no root Domain: *.com. - A Wildcard not matching a whole DNS label. e.g. *.foo.com and *.bar.foo.com are valid Wildcards however *bar.foo.com, *-bar.foo.com, and bar*.foo.com are all invalid. Additional notes: A Wildcard will not match empty string. e.g. *.foo.com will match bar.foo.com and baz-bar.foo.com but not .foo.com. The longest Wildcards match first. Only a single virtual host in the entire route configuration can match on *. Also a Domain must be unique across all virtual hosts within an advertise policy. Domains are also used for SNI matching if the Loadbalancer type is HTTPS. Domains also indicate the list of names for which DNS resolution will be automatically resolved to IP addresses by the system.
- `loadbalancer_type_choice` (Attributes) Proxy choice The type of load balancer, can be 'http' or 'https'<br>Exactly one of `http`, `https`, or `https_auto_cert` must be specified. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice))
- `name` (String) name This is the name of configuration object. It has to be unique within the namespace. It can only be specified during create API and cannot be changed during replace API. The value of name has to follow DNS-1035 format.
- `namespace` (String) namespace This defines the workspace within which each the configuration object is to be created. Must be a DNS_LABEL format. For a namespace object itself, namespace value will be ''

(see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_definition_choice))
- `api_protection_rules` (Attributes) API Protection rules API Protection Rules can be defined in two categories. The first category includes fine-grained rules, per API path and methods. The second category includes rules per API groups or Server URLs. If request matches any rule in the first category, second category rules are not evaluated. Rules can also include additional conditions, for example specific clients can access certain API endpoint or API group. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules))
- `blocked_clients` (Attributes List) Client Blocking Rules Define rules to block IP Prefixes or AS numbers. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--blocked_clients))
- `bot_defense_choice` (Attributes) Enable Bot Defense functionality for VirtualHost Bot Defense protects your applications from automated attacks by leveraging JavaScript and API calls to collect telemetry and mitigate sophisticated attacks within the context of F5's Distributed Cloud global network. When automation is detected, and mitigation action is set to Block or Redirect, the client will receive the configured mitigation response. If action is set to Flag, automated requests are monitored by Bot Defense, but are allowed to proceed to the customer's server.<br>Exactly one of `bot_defense`, `bot_defense_advanced_protection`, or `disable_bot_defense` must be specified when `bot_defense_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--bot_defense_choice))
- `bot_protection_choice` (Attributes) Enable Bot Protection functionality for VirtualHost Bot Protection for Distributed Cloud helps you protect entire web applications from automated threats and unwanted bot activity.<br>Exactly one of `bot_protection` or `disable_bot_protection` must be specified when `bot_protection_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--bot_protection_choice))
- `cache_options_choice` (Attributes) Enable CDN This feature belongs to the Content Delivery Network service. Enable it to enhance Console capabilities and utilize this feature.<br>Exactly one of `disable_caching` or `enable_cdn` must be specified when `cache_options_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--cache_options_choice))
- `challenge_type_choice` (Attributes) Challenge Type Malicious User Mitigation is an adaptive response and risk-based challenge capability. Enabling this feature would automatically serve different challenges such as JavaScript challenge, Captcha challenge or block temporarily based on the threat level of the malicious user. Policy based challenge can be used to selectively enable or disable JavaScript or Captcha challenge on a specific client and request match criteria<br>Exactly one of `captcha_challenge`, `enable_challenge`, `js_challenge`, `no_challenge`, or `policy_based_challenge` must be specified when `challenge_type_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--challenge_type_choice))
- `client_side_defense_choice` (Attributes) Enable Client-Side Defense functionality for VirtualHost Client-Side Defense (CSD) provides a multi-phase protection system that protects web applications against Magecart, formjacking, digital skimming, PII harvesting and other malicious JavaScript attacks. Enabling CSD is a 2-part process (1) Service Enablement (2) JavaScript injection using a Load Balancer. By clicking enable in this section and going through the configuration, you can complete part 2 of the process. To enable the service itself, please visit the Service's Landing page using the search on the left navigation pane.<br>Exactly one of `client_side_defense` or `disable_client_side_defense` must be specified when `client_side_defense_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--client_side_defense_choice))
- `cors_policy` (Attributes) Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) configuration for requests CORS is a mechanism that uses additional HTTP headers to tell a browser to let a web application running at one origin (domain) have permission to access selected resources from a server at a different origin (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--cors_policy))
- `csrf_policy` (Attributes) csrf_policy Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) is an attack that occurs when a malicious third-party website exploits a vulnerability thats allows them to submit an undesired request on user's behalf. The policy checks where a request is coming from to determine if the request's origin is the same as its destination. The policy relies on two pieces of information used in determining if a request originated from the same host. 1. The origin that caused the user agent to issue the request (source origin). 2. The origin that the request is going to (target origin). When the policy evaluating a request, it ensures both pieces of information are present and compare their values. If the source origin is missing or origins do not match the request is rejected. The exception to this being the source-origin has been added to the policy as valid. Because CSRF attacks specifically target state-changing requests, the policy only acts on the HTTP requests that have state-changing method (PUT,POST, etc.). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--csrf_policy))
- `data_guard_rules` (Attributes List) Data Guard Rules Data Guard prevents responses from exposing sensitive information by masking the data. The system masks credit card numbers and social security numbers leaked from the application from within the http response with a string of asterisks (*). Note: App Firewall should be enabled, to use Data Guard feature. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--data_guard_rules))
- `ddos_mitigation_rules` (Attributes List) DDoS Mitigation Rules Define manual mitigation rules to block L7 DDoS attacks. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--ddos_mitigation_rules))
- `default_route_pools` (Attributes List) Default Route Origin Pools Origin Pools used when no route is specified (default route) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--default_route_pools))
- `description` (String) description Human readable description for the object
- `graphql_rules` (Attributes List) GraphQL Inspection GraphQL is a query language and server-side runtime for APIs which provides a complete and understandable description of the data in API. GraphQL gives clients the power to ask for exactly what they need, makes it easier to evolve APIs over time, and enables powerful developer tools. Policy configuration to analyze GraphQL queries and prevent GraphQL tailored attacks. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--graphql_rules))
- `hash_policy_choice` (Attributes) Load Balancing Control The algorithm used to load balance requests between origin servers<br>Exactly one of `cookie_stickiness`, `least_active`, `random`, `ring_hash`, `round_robin`, or `source_ip_stickiness` must be specified when `hash_policy_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--hash_policy_choice))
- `ip_reputation_choice` (Attributes) ip_reputation IP reputation service analyzes IP threats and publishes a dynamic data set of millions of high-risk IP addresses, to protect users from inbound traffic from malicious IPs. IP threat categories include Spam Sources, Windows Exploits, Web Attacks, BotNets, Scanners, Denial of Service, Reputation, Phishing, Proxy, Mobile Threats, and TOR Proxy.<br>Exactly one of `disable_ip_reputation` or `enable_ip_reputation` must be specified when `ip_reputation_choice` is configured. - `jwt_validation` (Attributes) JWT Validation JWT Validation stops JWT replay attacks and JWT tampering by cryptographically verifying incoming JWTs before they are passed to origin APIs. - `l7_ddos_protection` (Attributes) L7 DDoS Protection Settings L7 DDoS protection is critical for safeguarding web applications, APIs, and services that are exposed to the internet from sophisticated, volumetric, application-level threats. Configure actions, thresholds and policies to apply during L7 DDoS attack (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--l7_ddos_protection))
- `labels` (Map of String) labels Map of string keys and values that can be used to organize and categorize (scope and select) objects as chosen by the user. Values specified here will be used by selector expression
- `malicious_user_detection_choice` (Attributes) Malicious User Detection Choice Malicious User Detection performs user behavior analysis and assigns a risk score and threat level of low, medium or high based on the suspicious activity of the user. The risk score of the user is decayed over time, if no further suspicious activity is noticed. The feature can be configured also via external app_type and labeling this HTTP Load Balancer. In this case external app_type configuration overrides internally disabled feature. Enabling the feature internally is allowed only when no labeling to external app_type.<br>Exactly one of `disable_malicious_user_detection` or `enable_malicious_user_detection` must be specified when `malicious_user_detection_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--malicious_user_detection_choice))
- `malware_protection_choice` (Attributes) Malware Protection Malware Protection protects Web Apps and APIs, from malicious file uploads by scanning files in real-time.<br>Exactly one of `disable_malware_protection` or `malware_protection_settings` must be specified when `malware_protection_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--malware_protection_choice))
- `more_option` (Attributes) More Options More options like header manipulation, compression etc. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--more_option))
- `origin_server_subset_rule_list` (Attributes) Origin Server Subset Rules Origin Server Subset Rules allow users to define match condition on Client (IP address, ASN, Country), IP Reputation, Regional Edge names, Request for subset selection of origin servers. Origin Server Subset  is a sequential engine where rules are evaluated one after the other. It's important to define the correct order for Origin Server Subset  to get the intended result, rules are evaluated from top to bottom in the list. When an Origin server subset rule is matched, then this selection rule takes effect and no more rules are evaluated. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--origin_server_subset_rule_list))
- `protected_cookies` (Attributes List) Cookie protection Allows setting attributes (SameSite, Secure, and HttpOnly) on cookies in responses. Cookie Tampering Protection prevents attackers from modifying the value of session cookies. For Cookie Tampering Protection, enabling a web app firewall (WAF) is a prerequisite. The configured mode of WAF (monitoring or blocking) will be enforced on the request when cookie tampering is identified. Note: We recommend enabling Secure and HttpOnly attributes along with cookie tampering protection. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--protected_cookies))
- `rate_limit_choice` (Attributes) Enable Rate Limiting Rate Limiting allows you to control the rate of requests sent to your origin servers, protect against API traffic surge and denial of services attacks.<br>Exactly one of `api_rate_limit`, `disable_rate_limit`, or `rate_limit` must be specified when `rate_limit_choice` is configured. - `sensitive_data_policy_choice` (Attributes) Sensitive Data Discovery Sensitive data discovery provide the ability to configure the policy for sensitive data detection<br>Exactly one of `default_sensitive_data_policy` or `sensitive_data_policy` must be specified when `sensitive_data_policy_choice` is configured. - `service_policy_choice` (Attributes) Service Policies Service policies provide the ability to configure security controls such as IP Allow/Deny lists, Geo IP filtering and Custom rules<br>Exactly one of `active_service_policies`, `no_service_policies`, or `service_policies_from_namespace` must be specified when `service_policy_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--service_policy_choice))
- `slow_ddos_mitigation_choice` (Attributes) Slow DDoS Mitigation 'Slow and low' attacks tie up server resources, leaving none available for servicing requests from actual users.Configuration that protects origins from slow and low attacks. In the case HTTP loadbalancer, only default settings can be applied. For HTTPS load balancer, the request timeout and request headers timeout value can be customized.<br>Exactly one of `slow_ddos_mitigation` or `system_default_timeouts` must be specified when `slow_ddos_mitigation_choice` is configured. - `threat_mesh_choice` (Attributes) threat_mesh Threat Mesh provides F5 Distributed Cloud customers with an additional layer of protection against web application attacks. Threat Mesh leverages cross-customer correlation (i.e. correlation of client attacks across different customers) to identify malicious intent of a client. Whenever a client is flagged due to a malicious intent by our WAAP decisions engines, that client will be added to the ThreatDB. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_testing_choice--api_testing--domains--credentials--credentials_choice--login_endpoint--json_payload--secret_info_choice))

Optional:

- `blindfold_secret_info` (Attributes) Blindfold Secret Blindfold Secret is used for the secrets managed by F5XC Secret Management Service<br>Conflicts with `clear_secret_info` and `none`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_testing_choice--api_testing--domains--credentials--credentials_choice--login_endpoint--json_payload--secret_info_choice--blindfold_secret_info))
- `clear_secret_info` (Attributes) Clear Secret Clear Secret is used for the secrets that are not encrypted<br>Conflicts with `blindfold_secret_info` and `none`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_testing_choice--api_testing--domains--credentials--credentials_choice--login_endpoint--json_payload--secret_info_choice--clear_secret_info))
- `none` (Boolean) None No private key will be stored or used. Choose this only when you need a public certificate for verification (e.g., validating SAML/JWT signatures). Not suitable for TLS or any use case that requires presenting a certificate, those will fail without a private key.<br>Conflicts with `blindfold_secret_info` and `clear_secret_info`.

<a id="nestedatt--api_testing_choice--api_testing--domains--credentials--credentials_choice--login_endpoint--json_payload--secret_info_choice--blindfold_secret_info"></a>

Required:

- `location` (String, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Location Location is the uri_ref. It could be in url format for string:/// Or it could be a path if the store provider is an http/https location

Optional:

- `decryption_provider` (String) Decryption Provider Name of the Secret Management Access object that contains information about the backend Secret Management service.
- `store_provider` (String) Store Provider Name of the Secret Management Access object that contains information about the store to get encrypted bytes This field needs to be provided only if the url scheme is not string:///

Required:

- `url` (String, Sensitive) URL URL of the secret. Currently supported URL schemes is string:///. For string:/// scheme, Secret needs to be encoded Base64 format. When asked for this secret, caller will get Secret bytes after Base64 decoding.

Optional:

- `provider` (String) Provider Name of the Secret Management Access object that contains information about the store to get encrypted bytes This field needs to be provided only if the url scheme is not string:///

<a id="nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `loadbalancer_type_choice`

Optional:

- `http` (Attributes) HTTP HTTP Load Balancer.<br>Conflicts with `https` and `https_auto_cert`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--http))
- `https` (Attributes) HTTPS HTTPS load balancer with a custom public/private certificate. This is also known as BYOC (Bring Your Own Certificate). User is responsible for managing DNS to this load balancer.<br>Conflicts with `http` and `https_auto_cert`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https))
- `https_auto_cert` (Attributes) HTTPS HTTPS load balancer with automatic public certificate provisioning. DNS records for the domains will be automatically managed by F5 Distributed Cloud. As a prerequisite, the domain must be delegated to F5 Distributed Cloud (see the DNS Management section) or a DNS CNAME record should be created in your DNS provider's portal(only for Domains not managed by F5 Distributed Cloud).<br>Conflicts with `http` and `https`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https_auto_cert))

### Nested Schema for `loadbalancer_type_choice.http`

Required:

- `port_choice` (Attributes) HTTP Port Choice Available options: user provided port or system default port or port range<br>Exactly one of `port` or `port_ranges` must be specified. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--http--port_choice))

Optional:

- `dns_volterra_managed` (Boolean) Manage DNS Domain DNS records for domains will be managed automatically by F5 Distributed Cloud. As a prerequisite, the domain must be delegated to F5 Distributed Cloud using Delegated domain feature or a DNS CNAME record should be created in your DNS provider's portal.<br>**Default:** `false`

Optional:

- `port` (Number) HTTP port to listen HTTP port to Listen.<br>Conflicts with `port_ranges`.
- `port_ranges` (String) Port_ranges A string containing a comma separated list of port ranges. Each port range consists of a single port or two ports separated by '-'.<br>**Validation:** `Length LengthBetween(1, 512)`<br>Conflicts with `port`.



<a id="nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https"></a>
### Nested Schema for `loadbalancer_type_choice.https`

Required:

- `port_choice` (Attributes) HTTPS Port Choice Available options: user provided port or system default port or port range<br>Exactly one of `port` or `port_ranges` must be specified. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--port_choice))
- `tls_certificates_choice` (Attributes) TLS Configuration TLS Certificate Configuration for downstream connections<br>Exactly one of `tls_cert_params` or `tls_parameters` must be specified. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--tls_certificates_choice))

Optional:

- `add_hsts` (Boolean) Add HSTS Add HTTP Strict-Transport-Security response header<br>**Default:** `false`
- `coalescing_options` (Attributes) TLS Coalescing options Options for coalescing TLS for multiple HTTPS Load Balancers (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--coalescing_options))
- `connection_idle_timeout` (Number) Connection Idle Timeout The idle timeout for downstream connections. The idle timeout is defined as the period in which there are no active requests. When the idle timeout is reached the connection will be closed. Note that request based timeouts mean that HTTP/2 PINGs will not keep the connection alive. This is specified in milliseconds. The default value is 2 minutes.<br>**Default:** `0`
- `default_lb_choice` (Attributes) Default Load Balancer Designate the Load balancer as default for clients that don't present the SNI header in TLS handshake.<br>Exactly one of `default_loadbalancer` or `non_default_loadbalancer` must be specified when `default_lb_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--default_lb_choice))
- `http_protocol_options` (Attributes) http_protocol_options HTTP protocol configuration options for downstream connections. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--http_protocol_options))
- `http_redirect` (Boolean) HTTP Redirect Redirect HTTP traffic to HTTPS<br>**Default:** `false`
- `path_normalize_choice` (Attributes) Normalize Path URI Path is normalized and adjacent slashes in the path are merged into one. The platform does not perform case normalization.<br>Exactly one of `disable_path_normalize` or `enable_path_normalize` must be specified when `path_normalize_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--path_normalize_choice))
- `server_header_choice` (Attributes) Server Header configuration Define the settings of “server” response header. A response header with name “server” and value “volt-adc” is added to responses by default.<br>Exactly one of `append_server_name`, `default_header`, `pass_through`, or `server_name` must be specified when `server_header_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--server_header_choice))

- `provider` (String) Provider Name of the Secret Management Access object that contains information about the store to get encrypted bytes This field needs to be provided only if the url scheme is not string:///




<a id="nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--tls_certificates_choice--tls_parameters--tls_certificates--ocsp_stapling_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `loadbalancer_type_choice.https.tls_certificates_choice.tls_parameters.tls_certificates.ocsp_stapling_choice`

Optional:

- `custom_hash_algorithms` (Attributes) Use Custom Order for Hash Algorithms Use hash algorithms in the custom order. F5XC will try to fetch ocsp response from the CA in the given order. Additionally, LoadBalancer will not become active until ocspResponse cannot be fetched if the certificate has MustStaple extension set.<br>Conflicts with `disable_ocsp_stapling` and `use_system_defaults`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--tls_certificates_choice--tls_parameters--tls_certificates--ocsp_stapling_choice--custom_hash_algorithms))
- `disable_ocsp_stapling` (Boolean) Disable OCSP Stapling Disable OCSP Stapling. F5XC will not fetch and staple OCSP Response for this certificate. This is the default behavior if no choice is selected.<br>Conflicts with `custom_hash_algorithms` and `use_system_defaults`.
- `use_system_defaults` (Boolean) Fetch with F5XC default settings Use F5XC Default Settings to fetch and staple OCSP Response. OCSP Response will be stapled if it can be fetched. Additionally, LoadBalancer will not become active until ocspResponse cannot be fetched if the certificate has MustStaple extension set. F5XC will try to fetch OCSPResponse with sha256 and sha1 as HashAlgorithm, in that order.<br>Conflicts with `custom_hash_algorithms` and `disable_ocsp_stapling`.

<a id="nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--tls_certificates_choice--tls_parameters--tls_certificates--ocsp_stapling_choice--custom_hash_algorithms"></a>
### Nested Schema for `loadbalancer_type_choice.https.tls_certificates_choice.tls_parameters.tls_certificates.ocsp_stapling_choice.custom_hash_algorithms`

Required:

- `hash_algorithms` (List of String) Hash Algorithms Ordered list of hash algorithms to be used.<br>**Valid Options:** `['SHA1', 'SHA256']` (Multiple selection allowed)

<a id="nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--tls_certificates_choice--tls_parameters--tls_config"></a>
### Nested Schema for `loadbalancer_type_choice.https.tls_certificates_choice.tls_parameters.tls_config`

Optional:

- `choice` (Attributes) TLS Security Level The security level for TLS handshake between client/server and the platform.<br>Exactly one of `custom_security`, `default_security`, `low_security`, or `medium_security` must be specified when `choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--tls_certificates_choice--tls_parameters--tls_config--choice))

<a id="nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--tls_certificates_choice--tls_parameters--tls_config--choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `loadbalancer_type_choice.https.tls_certificates_choice.tls_parameters.tls_config.choice`

Optional:

- `custom_security` (Attributes) Custom Security Custom selection of TLS versions and cipher suites<br>Conflicts with `default_security`, `low_security`, and `medium_security`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--tls_certificates_choice--tls_parameters--tls_config--choice--custom_security))
- `default_security` (Boolean) Default Security TLS v1.2+ with PFS ciphers and strong crypto algorithms.<br>Conflicts with `custom_security`, `low_security`, and `medium_security`.
- `low_security` (Boolean) Low Security TLS v1.0+ including non-PFS ciphers and weak crypto algorithms.<br>Conflicts with `custom_security`, `default_security`, and `medium_security`.
- `medium_security` (Boolean) Medium Security TLS v1.0+ with PFS ciphers and medium strength crypto algorithms.<br>Conflicts with `custom_security`, `default_security`, and `low_security`.

<a id="nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--tls_certificates_choice--tls_parameters--tls_config--choice--custom_security"></a>
### Nested Schema for `loadbalancer_type_choice.https.tls_certificates_choice.tls_parameters.tls_config.choice.custom_security`

Required:

- `cipher_suites` (List of String) cipher_suites The TLS listener will only support the specified cipher list.<br>**Valid Options:** `['TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256', 'TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384', 'TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256', 'TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256', 'TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384', 'TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256', 'TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256', 'TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384', 'TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256', 'TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA', 'TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA', 'TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA', 'TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA', 'TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA', 'TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256', 'TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_256_CBC_SHA', 'TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384']` (Multiple selection allowed)

Optional:

- `max_version` (List of String) maximum_protocol_version Maximum TLS protocol version.<br>**Allowed Values (choose one):** `['TLS_AUTO', 'TLSv1_0', 'TLSv1_1', 'TLSv1_2', 'TLSv1_3']`<br>**Default:** `TLS_AUTO`
- `min_version` (List of String) minimum_protocol_version Minimum TLS protocol version.<br>**Allowed Values (choose one):** `['TLS_AUTO', 'TLSv1_0', 'TLSv1_1', 'TLSv1_2', 'TLSv1_3']`<br>**Default:** `TLS_AUTO`

<a id="nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--http_protocol_options"></a>
### Nested Schema for `loadbalancer_type_choice.https.http_protocol_options`

Optional:

- `http_protocol_choice` (Attributes) HTTP Protocol Configuration HTTP protocol configuration options for downstream connections<br>Exactly one of `http_protocol_enable_v1_only`, `http_protocol_enable_v1_v2`, or `http_protocol_enable_v2_only` must be specified when `http_protocol_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--http_protocol_options--http_protocol_choice))

<a id="nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--http_protocol_options--http_protocol_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `loadbalancer_type_choice.https.http_protocol_options.http_protocol_choice`

Optional:

- `http_protocol_enable_v1_only` (Attributes) http_protocol_enable_v1_only Enable HTTP/1.1 for downstream connections<br>Conflicts with `http_protocol_enable_v1_v2` and `http_protocol_enable_v2_only`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--http_protocol_options--http_protocol_choice--http_protocol_enable_v1_only))
- `http_protocol_enable_v1_v2` (Boolean) http_protocol_enable_v1_v2 Enable both HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 for downstream connections<br>Conflicts with `http_protocol_enable_v1_only` and `http_protocol_enable_v2_only`.
- `http_protocol_enable_v2_only` (Boolean) http_protocol_enable_v2_only Enable HTTP/2 for downstream connections<br>Conflicts with `http_protocol_enable_v1_only` and `http_protocol_enable_v1_v2`.

<a id="nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--http_protocol_options--http_protocol_choice--http_protocol_enable_v1_only"></a>
### Nested Schema for `loadbalancer_type_choice.https.http_protocol_options.http_protocol_choice.http_protocol_enable_v1_only`

Optional:

- `header_transformation` (Attributes) Header transformation Two mutually exclusive types of header key formatters are supported: Stateless (Default and Proper Case) and Stateful (Preserve Case) formatters. When a Stateless formatter is selected, it applies to response headers sent to the client and when a Stateful formatter is selected, it applies to the upstream request headers. It's essential to ensure that the same formatter type (either stateless or stateful) is applied on origin pool. If different formatter types are applied, only the stateful formatter will take effect, and the stateless formatter will be disregarded. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--http_protocol_options--http_protocol_choice--http_protocol_enable_v1_only--header_transformation))

<a id="nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--http_protocol_options--http_protocol_choice--http_protocol_enable_v1_only--header_transformation"></a>
### Nested Schema for `loadbalancer_type_choice.https.http_protocol_options.http_protocol_choice.http_protocol_enable_v1_only.header_transformation`

Optional:

- `header_transformation_choice` (Attributes) Header transformation Select header transformation options for HTTP/1.1<br>Exactly one of `default_header_transformation`, `legacy_header_transformation`, `preserve_case_header_transformation`, or `proper_case_header_transformation` must be specified when `header_transformation_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--http_protocol_options--http_protocol_choice--http_protocol_enable_v1_only--header_transformation--header_transformation_choice))

<a id="nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--http_protocol_options--http_protocol_choice--http_protocol_enable_v1_only--header_transformation--header_transformation_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `loadbalancer_type_choice.https.http_protocol_options.http_protocol_choice.http_protocol_enable_v1_only.header_transformation.header_transformation_choice`

Optional:

- `default_header_transformation` (Boolean) Default header transformation Normalize the headers to lower case<br>Conflicts with `legacy_header_transformation`, `preserve_case_header_transformation`, and `proper_case_header_transformation`.
- `legacy_header_transformation` (Boolean) Legacy header transformations Use old header transformation if configured earlier<br>Conflicts with `default_header_transformation`, `preserve_case_header_transformation`, and `proper_case_header_transformation`.
- `preserve_case_header_transformation` (Boolean) Preserve case header transformation Preserves the original case of headers without any modifications.<br>Conflicts with `default_header_transformation`, `legacy_header_transformation`, and `proper_case_header_transformation`.
- `proper_case_header_transformation` (Boolean) Proper case header transformation Normalize the headers to proper case words. The first character and any character following a special character will be capitalized if it’s an alpha character. For example, “content-type” becomes “Content-Type”, and “foo$b#$are” becomes “Foo$B#$Are”<br>Conflicts with `default_header_transformation`, `legacy_header_transformation`, and `preserve_case_header_transformation`.






<a id="nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--path_normalize_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `loadbalancer_type_choice.https.path_normalize_choice`

Optional:

- `disable_path_normalize` (Boolean) Disable Path normalization<br>Conflicts with `enable_path_normalize`.
- `enable_path_normalize` (Boolean) Enable Path normalization<br>Conflicts with `disable_path_normalize`.


<a id="nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https--server_header_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `loadbalancer_type_choice.https.server_header_choice`

Optional:

- `append_server_name` (String) append_server_name Define the header value for the header name 'server'. If header value is already present, it is not overwritten and passed as-is.<br>**Validation:** `Length LengthAtMost(8096)`<br>Conflicts with `default_header`, `pass_through`, and `server_name`.
- `default_header` (Boolean) default_header Response header name is 'server' and value is 'volt-adc'<br>Conflicts with `append_server_name`, `pass_through`, and `server_name`.
- `pass_through` (Boolean) pass_through Pass existing server header as is. If server header is absent, a new header is not appended.<br>Conflicts with `append_server_name`, `default_header`, and `server_name`.
- `server_name` (String) server_name Define the header value for the header name 'server'. This will overwrite existing values, if any, for the server header.<br>**Validation:** `Length LengthAtMost(8096)`<br>Conflicts with `append_server_name`, `default_header`, and `pass_through`.



<a id="nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https_auto_cert"></a>
### Nested Schema for `loadbalancer_type_choice.https_auto_cert`

Optional:

- `add_hsts` (Boolean) Add HSTS Add HTTP Strict-Transport-Security response header<br>**Default:** `false`
- `coalescing_options` (Attributes) TLS Coalescing options Options for coalescing TLS for multiple HTTPS Load Balancers (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https_auto_cert--coalescing_options))
- `connection_idle_timeout` (Number) Connection Idle Timeout The idle timeout for downstream connections. The idle timeout is defined as the period in which there are no active requests. When the idle timeout is reached the connection will be closed. Note that request based timeouts mean that HTTP/2 PINGs will not keep the connection alive. This is specified in milliseconds. The default value is 2 minutes.<br>**Default:** `120000`
- `default_lb_choice` (Attributes) Default Load Balancer For clients that don't specify the SNI field in the TLS handshake, designate this Load Balancer as default among any listening on the same VIP and port.<br>Exactly one of `default_loadbalancer` or `non_default_loadbalancer` must be specified when `default_lb_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https_auto_cert--default_lb_choice))
- `http_protocol_options` (Attributes) http_protocol_options HTTP protocol configuration options for downstream connections. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https_auto_cert--http_protocol_options))
- `http_redirect` (Boolean) HTTP Redirect Redirect HTTP traffic to HTTPS<br>**Default:** `false`
- `mtls_choice` (Attributes) mTLS choice mTLS authentication between clients and HTTPS load balancer<br>Exactly one of `no_mtls` or `use_mtls` must be specified when `mtls_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https_auto_cert--mtls_choice))
- `path_normalize_choice` (Attributes) Normalize Path URI Path is normalized and adjacent slashes in the path are merged into one. The platform does not perform case normalization.<br>Exactly one of `disable_path_normalize` or `enable_path_normalize` must be specified when `path_normalize_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https_auto_cert--path_normalize_choice))
- `port_choice` (Attributes) HTTPS Port Choice Available options: user provided port or system default port or port range<br>Exactly one of `port` or `port_ranges` must be specified when `port_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https_auto_cert--port_choice))
- `server_header_choice` (Attributes) Server Header configuration Define the settings of “server” response header. A response header with name “server” and value “volt-adc” is added to responses by default.<br>Exactly one of `append_server_name`, `default_header`, `pass_through`, or `server_name` must be specified when `server_header_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https_auto_cert--server_header_choice))
- `tls_config` (Attributes) TLS Config Configuration of TLS settings such as min/max TLS version and ciphersuites (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https_auto_cert--tls_config))

It's essential to ensure that the same formatter type (either stateless or stateful) is applied on origin pool. If different formatter types are applied, only the stateful formatter will take effect, and the stateless formatter will be disregarded. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https_auto_cert--http_protocol_options--http_protocol_choice--http_protocol_enable_v1_only--header_transformation))

- `header_transformation_choice` (Attributes) Header transformation Select header transformation options for HTTP/1.1<br>Exactly one of `default_header_transformation`, `legacy_header_transformation`, `preserve_case_header_transformation`, or `proper_case_header_transformation` must be specified when `header_transformation_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--loadbalancer_type_choice--https_auto_cert--http_protocol_options--http_protocol_choice--http_protocol_enable_v1_only--header_transformation--header_transformation_choice))

Optional:

- `default_header_transformation` (Boolean) Default header transformation Normalize the headers to lower case<br>Conflicts with `legacy_header_transformation`, `preserve_case_header_transformation`, and `proper_case_header_transformation`.
- `legacy_header_transformation` (Boolean) Legacy header transformations Use old header transformation if configured earlier<br>Conflicts with `default_header_transformation`, `preserve_case_header_transformation`, and `proper_case_header_transformation`.
- `preserve_case_header_transformation` (Boolean) Preserve case header transformation Preserves the original case of headers without any modifications.<br>Conflicts with `default_header_transformation`, `legacy_header_transformation`, and `proper_case_header_transformation`.
- `proper_case_header_transformation` (Boolean) Proper case header transformation Normalize the headers to proper case words. The first character and any character following a special character will be capitalized if it’s an alpha character. For example, “content-type” becomes “Content-Type”, and “foo$b#$are” becomes “Foo$B#$Are”<br>Conflicts with `default_header_transformation`, `legacy_header_transformation`, and `preserve_case_header_transformation`.

Optional:

- `methods` (List of String) Methods Methods to be matched<br>**Valid Options:** `['ANY', 'CONNECT', 'COPY', 'DELETE', 'GET', 'HEAD', 'OPTIONS', 'PATCH', 'POST', 'PUT', 'TRACE']` (Multiple selection allowed)



<a id="nestedatt--api_definition_choice--api_specification--validation_target_choice--validation_all_spec_endpoints--fall_through_mode--fall_through_mode_choice--fall_through_mode_custom--open_api_validation_rules--metadata"></a>

Required:

- `name` (String) name This is the name of the message. The value of name has to follow DNS-1035 format.<br>**Validation:** `Length LengthAtLeast(1)`

Optional:

- `description` (String) description Human readable description.<br>**Validation:** `Length LengthAtMost(256)`


<a id="nestedatt--api_definition_choice--api_specification--validation_target_choice--validation_all_spec_endpoints--fall_through_mode--fall_through_mode_choice--fall_through_mode_custom--open_api_validation_rules--action_choice"></a>

- `action_block` (Boolean) block Block the request and issue an API security event<br>Conflicts with `action_report` and `action_skip`.
- `action_report` (Boolean) report Continue processing the request and issue an API security event<br>Conflicts with `action_block` and `action_skip`.
- `action_skip` (Boolean) skip Continue processing the request<br>Conflicts with `action_block` and `action_report`.

Required:

Indicates if enforcement is needed when a validation mismatch occurs on a request to one of the endpoints listed on the OpenAPI specification file (a.k.a. swagger)<br>Exactly one of `skip_validation` or `validation_mode_active` must be specified. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_definition_choice--api_specification--validation_target_choice--validation_all_spec_endpoints--validation_mode--validation_mode_choice))

Optional:

- `response_validation_mode_choice` (Attributes) Response Validation Mode Choice Validation mode of OpenAPI specification response. Indicates if enforcement is needed when a validation mismatch occurs on a response to one of the endpoints listed on the OpenAPI specification file (a.k.a. swagger)<br>Exactly one of `response_validation_mode_active` or `skip_response_validation` must be specified when `response_validation_mode_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_definition_choice--api_specification--validation_target_choice--validation_all_spec_endpoints--validation_mode--response_validation_mode_choice))

<a id="nestedatt--api_definition_choice--api_specification--validation_target_choice--validation_all_spec_endpoints--validation_mode--validation_mode_choice"></a>

Optional:

- `response_validation_properties` (List of String) Response Validation Properties List of properties of the response to validate according to the OpenAPI specification file (a.k.a. swagger)<br>**Valid Options:** `['PROPERTY_CONTENT_TYPE', 'PROPERTY_COOKIE_PARAMETERS', 'PROPERTY_HTTP_BODY', 'PROPERTY_HTTP_HEADERS', 'PROPERTY_PATH_PARAMETERS', 'PROPERTY_QUERY_PARAMETERS', 'PROPERTY_RESPONSE_CODE', 'PROPERTY_SECURITY_SCHEMA']` (Multiple selection allowed)<br>**Default:** `PROPERTY_HTTP_HEADERS`
- `validation_enforcement_type_choice` (Attributes) Response Validation Enforcement Mode Enforcement type of OpenAPI specification for the response<br>Exactly one of `enforcement_block` or `enforcement_report` must be specified when `validation_enforcement_type_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_definition_choice--api_specification--validation_target_choice--validation_custom_list--open_api_validation_rules--validation_mode--response_validation_mode_choice--response_validation_mode_active--validation_enforcement_type_choice))

- `enforcement_report` (Boolean) Report Allow the response, trigger an API security event<br>Conflicts with `enforcement_block`.

(see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_definition_choice--api_specification--validation_target_choice--validation_custom_list--settings--oversized_body_choice))

<a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules`

Optional:

- `api_endpoint_rules` (Attributes List) api_endpoint_rules This category defines specific rules per API endpoints. If request matches any of these rules, skipping second category rules. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules))
- `api_groups_rules` (Attributes List) api_groups_rules This category includes rules per API group or Server URL. For API groups, refer to API Definition which includes API groups derived from uploaded swaggers. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_groups_rules))

<a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules.api_endpoint_rules`

Required:

- `action` (Attributes) action The action to take if the input request matches the rule. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--action))
- `api_endpoint_path` (String) api endpoint path The endpoint (path) of the request.<br>**Validation:** `Length LengthAtMost(1024)`
- `metadata` (Attributes) metadata Common attributes for the rule including name and description. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--metadata))

Optional:

- `api_endpoint_method` (Attributes) method The list of expected values for the HTTP method in the request API. The actual value of the HTTP method is extracted from the HTTP request. The predicate evaluates to true if the actual HTTP method belongs is present in the list of expected values. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--api_endpoint_method))
- `client_matcher` (Attributes) client_matcher Conditions related to the origin of the request, such as client IP, TLS fingerprint, etc. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher))
- `domain_choice` (Attributes) domain choices Choose if the rule will apply for all domains or a specific one.<br>Exactly one of `any_domain` or `specific_domain` must be specified when `domain_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--domain_choice))
- `request_matcher` (Attributes) request_matcher Conditions related to the request, such as query parameters, headers, etc. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--request_matcher))

<a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--action"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules.api_endpoint_rules.action`

Optional:

- `action_choice` (Attributes) action The action to take when rule is matched.<br>Exactly one of `allow` or `deny` must be specified when `action_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--action--action_choice))

<a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--action--action_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules.api_endpoint_rules.action.action_choice`

Optional:

- `allow` (Boolean) Allow Allow the request to proceed.<br>Conflicts with `deny`.
- `deny` (Boolean) Deny Deny the request.<br>Conflicts with `allow`.



<a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--metadata"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules.api_endpoint_rules.metadata`

Required:

- `name` (String) name This is the name of the message. The value of name has to follow DNS-1035 format.<br>**Validation:** `Length LengthAtLeast(1)`

Optional:

- `description` (String) description Human readable description.<br>**Validation:** `Length LengthAtMost(256)`


<a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--api_endpoint_method"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules.api_endpoint_rules.api_endpoint_method`

Optional:

- `invert_matcher` (Boolean) invert_matcher Invert the match result.<br>**Default:** `false`
- `methods` (List of String) methods List of methods values to match against.<br>**Valid Options:** `['ANY', 'CONNECT', 'COPY', 'DELETE', 'GET', 'HEAD', 'OPTIONS', 'PATCH', 'POST', 'PUT', 'TRACE']` (Multiple selection allowed)


<a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules.api_endpoint_rules.client_matcher`

Optional:

- `client_choice` (Attributes) client choice Select clients for which the rule will be applied. The actual names of the client are extracted from its TLS certificate.<br>Exactly one of `any_client`, `client_selector`, or `ip_threat_category_list` must be specified when `client_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--client_choice))
- `ip_asn_choice` (Attributes) ip asn choice Match source IP address/ASN  of the request<br>Exactly one of `any_ip`, `asn_list`, `asn_matcher`, `ip_matcher`, or `ip_prefix_list` must be specified when `ip_asn_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--ip_asn_choice))
- `tls_fingerprint_matcher` (Attributes) TLS JA3 fingerprint matcher TLS JA3 fingerprints to be matched. The predicate evaluates to true if the TLS fingerprint matches any of the exact values or classes of known TLS fingerprints. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--tls_fingerprint_matcher))

<a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--client_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules.api_endpoint_rules.client_matcher.client_choice`

Optional:

- `any_client` (Boolean) any ip Any Client<br>Conflicts with `client_selector` and `ip_threat_category_list`.
- `client_selector` (Attributes) client selector A label selector that describes the expected set of clients. The labels associated with the client making the API request are used to evaluate the label expressions in the selector. These labels can be derived from the client TLS certificate or from the volterra internal control plane. This is a more flexible and powerful version of the client name matcher predicate that allows a given rule to be applicable to a set of clients based on the client labels rather than being limited to relying on patterns in the client name. The predicate evaluates to true if the expressions in the label selector are true for the client labels.<br>Conflicts with `any_client` and `ip_threat_category_list`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--client_choice--client_selector))
- `ip_threat_category_list` (Attributes) IP Threat Category List IP threat categories to choose from<br>Conflicts with `any_client` and `client_selector`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--client_choice--ip_threat_category_list))

<a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--client_choice--client_selector"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules.api_endpoint_rules.client_matcher.client_choice.client_selector`

Required:

- `expressions` (List of String) expressions expressions contains the kubernetes style label expression for selections.


<a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--client_choice--ip_threat_category_list"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules.api_endpoint_rules.client_matcher.client_choice.ip_threat_category_list`

Required:

- `ip_threat_categories` (List of String) IP Threat Categories The IP threat categories is obtained from the list and is used to auto-generate equivalent label selection expressions<br>**Valid Options:** `['BOTNETS', 'DENIAL_OF_SERVICE', 'MOBILE_THREATS', 'NETWORK', 'PHISHING', 'PROXY', 'REPUTATION', 'SCANNERS', 'SPAM_SOURCES', 'TOR_PROXY', 'WEB_ATTACKS', 'WINDOWS_EXPLOITS']` (Multiple selection allowed)



<a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--ip_asn_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules.api_endpoint_rules.client_matcher.ip_asn_choice`

Optional:

- `any_ip` (Boolean) any ip Any Source IP<br>Conflicts with `asn_list`, `asn_matcher`, `ip_matcher`, and `ip_prefix_list`.
- `asn_list` (Attributes) asn list List of 4-byte ASN values. The predicate evaluates to true if the origin ASN is present in the ASN list.<br>Conflicts with `any_ip`, `asn_matcher`, `ip_matcher`, and `ip_prefix_list`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--ip_asn_choice--asn_list))
- `asn_matcher` (Attributes) asn matcher List of references to BGP ASN Set objects. The predicate evaluates to true if the origin ASN is present in one of the BGP ASN Set objects.<br>Conflicts with `any_ip`, `asn_list`, `ip_matcher`, and `ip_prefix_list`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--ip_asn_choice--asn_matcher))
- `ip_matcher` (Attributes) ip matcher List of references to IP Prefix Set objects. The predicate evaluates to true if the client IP Address is covered by one or more of the IP Prefixes in the IP Prefix Sets.<br>Conflicts with `any_ip`, `asn_list`, `asn_matcher`, and `ip_prefix_list`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--ip_asn_choice--ip_matcher))
- `ip_prefix_list` (Attributes) ip prefix list List of IP Prefixes values. The predicate evaluates to true if the client IP Address is covered by one or more of the IP Prefixes from the list.<br>Conflicts with `any_ip`, `asn_list`, `asn_matcher`, and `ip_matcher`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--ip_asn_choice--ip_prefix_list))

<a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--ip_asn_choice--asn_list"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules.api_endpoint_rules.client_matcher.ip_asn_choice.asn_list`

Required:

- `as_numbers` (List of Number) as numbers An unordered set of RFC 6793 defined 4-byte AS numbers that can be used to create allow or deny lists for use in network policy or service policy. It can be used to create the allow list only for DNS Load Balancer.


<a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--ip_asn_choice--asn_matcher"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules.api_endpoint_rules.client_matcher.ip_asn_choice.asn_matcher`

Required:

- `asn_sets` (Attributes List) asn_sets A list of references to bgp_asn_set objects. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--ip_asn_choice--asn_matcher--asn_sets))

<a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--ip_asn_choice--asn_matcher--asn_sets"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules.api_endpoint_rules.client_matcher.ip_asn_choice.asn_matcher.asn_sets`

Required:

- `name` (String)
- `namespace` (String)

Optional:

- `tenant` (String)



<a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--ip_asn_choice--ip_matcher"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules.api_endpoint_rules.client_matcher.ip_asn_choice.ip_matcher`

Required:

- `prefix_sets` (Attributes List) prefix_sets A list of references to ip_prefix_set objects. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--ip_asn_choice--ip_matcher--prefix_sets))

Optional:

- `invert_matcher` (Boolean) invert_matcher Invert the match result.<br>**Default:** `false`

<a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--ip_asn_choice--ip_matcher--prefix_sets"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules.api_endpoint_rules.client_matcher.ip_asn_choice.ip_matcher.prefix_sets`

Required:

- `name` (String)
- `namespace` (String)

Optional:

- `tenant` (String)



<a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--ip_asn_choice--ip_prefix_list"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules.api_endpoint_rules.client_matcher.ip_asn_choice.ip_prefix_list`

Optional:

- `invert_match` (Boolean) invert_matcher Invert the match result.<br>**Default:** `false`
- `ip_prefixes` (List of String) ip prefixes List of IPv4 prefix strings.
- `ipv6_prefixes` (List of String) ipv6 prefixes List of IPv6 prefix strings.



<a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--tls_fingerprint_matcher"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules.api_endpoint_rules.client_matcher.tls_fingerprint_matcher`

Optional:

- `classes` (List of String) classes A list of known classes of TLS fingerprints to match the input TLS JA3 fingerprint against.<br>**Valid Options:** `['ADWARE', 'ADWIND', 'ANY_MALICIOUS_FINGERPRINT', 'DRIDEX', 'GOOTKIT', 'GOZI', 'JBIFROST', 'QUAKBOT', 'RANSOMWARE', 'TOFSEE', 'TORRENTLOCKER', 'TRICKBOT', 'TROLDESH']` (Multiple selection allowed)
- `exact_values` (List of String) exact values A list of exact TLS JA3 fingerprints to match the input TLS JA3 fingerprint against.
- `excluded_values` (List of String) excluded values A list of TLS JA3 fingerprints to be excluded when matching the input TLS JA3 fingerprint. This can be used to skip known false positives when using one or more known TLS fingerprint classes in the enclosing matcher.



<a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--domain_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules.api_endpoint_rules.domain_choice`

Optional:

- `any_domain` (Boolean) any domain The rule will apply for all domains.<br>Conflicts with `specific_domain`.
- `specific_domain` (String) domain The rule will apply for a specific domain. For example: api.example.com<br>**Validation:** `Length LengthAtMost(128)`<br>Conflicts with `any_domain`.


<a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--request_matcher"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules.api_endpoint_rules.request_matcher`

Optional:

- `cookie_matchers` (Attributes List) cookie matchers A list of predicates for all cookies that need to be matched. The criteria for matching each cookie is described in individual instances of CookieMatcherType. The actual cookie values are extracted from the request API as a list of strings for each cookie name. Note that all specified cookie matcher predicates must evaluate to true. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--request_matcher--cookie_matchers))
- `headers` (Attributes List) headers A list of predicates for various HTTP headers that need to match. The criteria for matching each HTTP header are described in individual HeaderMatcherType instances. The actual HTTP header values are extracted from the request API as a list of strings for each HTTP header type. Note that all specified header predicates must evaluate to true. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--request_matcher--headers))
- `jwt_claims` (Attributes List) JWT claims A list of predicates for various JWT claims that need to match. The criteria for matching each JWT claim are described in individual JWTClaimMatcherType instances. The actual JWT claims values are extracted from the JWT payload as a list of strings. Note that all specified JWT claim predicates must evaluate to true. Note that this feature only works on LBs with JWT Validation feature enabled. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--request_matcher--jwt_claims))
- `query_params` (Attributes List) query params A list of predicates for all query parameters that need to be matched. The criteria for matching each query parameter are described in individual instances of QueryParameterMatcherType. The actual query parameter values are extracted from the request API as a list of strings for each query parameter name. Note that all specified query parameter predicates must evaluate to true. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--request_matcher--query_params))

<a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--request_matcher--cookie_matchers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules.api_endpoint_rules.request_matcher.cookie_matchers`

Required:

- `match_choice` (Attributes) match Select Match Options.<br>Exactly one of `check_not_present`, `check_present`, or `item` must be specified. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--request_matcher--cookie_matchers--match_choice))
- `name` (String) name A case-sensitive cookie name.

Optional:

- `invert_matcher` (Boolean) invert_matcher Invert Match of the expression defined<br>**Default:** `false`

<a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--request_matcher--cookie_matchers--match_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules.api_endpoint_rules.request_matcher.cookie_matchers.match_choice`

Optional:

- `check_not_present` (Boolean) check_not_present Check that the cookie is not present.<br>Conflicts with `check_present` and `item`.
- `check_present` (Boolean) check_present Check that the cookie is present.<br>Conflicts with `check_not_present` and `item`.
- `item` (Attributes) item Criteria for matching the values for the cookie. The match is successful if any of the values in the input satisfies the criteria in the matcher.<br>Conflicts with `check_not_present` and `check_present`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--request_matcher--cookie_matchers--match_choice--item))

<a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--request_matcher--cookie_matchers--match_choice--item"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules.api_endpoint_rules.request_matcher.cookie_matchers.match_choice.item`

Optional:

- `exact_values` (List of String) exact values A list of exact values to match the input against.
- `regex_values` (List of String) regex values A list of regular expressions to match the input against.
- `transformers` (List of String) transformers An ordered list of transformers (starting from index 0) to be applied to the path before matching.<br>**Valid Options:** `['BASE64_DECODE', 'LOWER_CASE', 'NORMALIZE_PATH', 'REMOVE_WHITESPACE', 'TRANSFORMER_NONE', 'TRIM', 'TRIM_LEFT', 'TRIM_RIGHT', 'UPPER_CASE', 'URL_DECODE']` (Multiple selection allowed)




<a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--request_matcher--headers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules.api_endpoint_rules.request_matcher.headers`

Required:

- `match_choice` (Attributes) match Select Match Options.<br>Exactly one of `check_not_present`, `check_present`, or `item` must be specified. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--request_matcher--headers--match_choice))
- `name` (String) name A case-insensitive HTTP header name.

Optional:

- `invert_matcher` (Boolean) invert_matcher Invert the match result.<br>**Default:** `false`

<a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_endpoint_rules--request_matcher--headers--match_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules.api_endpoint_rules.request_matcher.headers.match_choice`

Optional:

- `check_not_present` (Boolean) check_not_present Check that the header is not present.<br>Conflicts with `check_present` and `item`.
- `check_present` (Boolean) check_present Check that the header is present.<br>Conflicts with `check_not_present` and `item`.
- `item` (Attributes) item Criteria for matching the values for the header. The match is successful if any of the values in the input satisfies the criteria in the matcher.<br>Conflicts with `check_not_present` and `check_present`. <a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_groups_rules--client_matcher"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules.api_groups_rules.client_matcher`

Optional:

- `client_choice` (Attributes) client choice Select clients for which the rule will be applied. The actual names of the client are extracted from its TLS certificate.<br>Exactly one of `any_client`, `client_selector`, or `ip_threat_category_list` must be specified when `client_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_groups_rules--client_matcher--client_choice))
- `ip_asn_choice` (Attributes) ip asn choice Match source IP address/ASN  of the request<br>Exactly one of `any_ip`, `asn_list`, `asn_matcher`, `ip_matcher`, or `ip_prefix_list` must be specified when `ip_asn_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_groups_rules--client_matcher--ip_asn_choice))
- `tls_fingerprint_matcher` (Attributes) TLS JA3 fingerprint matcher TLS JA3 fingerprints to be matched. The predicate evaluates to true if the TLS fingerprint matches any of the exact values or classes of known TLS fingerprints. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_groups_rules--client_matcher--tls_fingerprint_matcher))

<a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_groups_rules--client_matcher--client_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules.api_groups_rules.client_matcher.client_choice`

Optional:

- `any_client` (Boolean) any ip Any Client<br>Conflicts with `client_selector` and `ip_threat_category_list`.
- `client_selector` (Attributes) client selector A label selector that describes the expected set of clients. The labels associated with the client making the API request are used to evaluate the label expressions in the selector. These labels can be derived from the client TLS certificate or from the volterra internal control plane. This is a more flexible and powerful version of the client name matcher predicate that allows a given rule to be applicable to a set of clients based on the client labels rather than being limited to relying on patterns in the client name. The predicate evaluates to true if the expressions in the label selector are true for the client labels.<br>Conflicts with `any_client` and `ip_threat_category_list`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_groups_rules--client_matcher--client_choice--client_selector))
- `ip_threat_category_list` (Attributes) IP Threat Category List IP threat categories to choose from<br>Conflicts with `any_client` and `client_selector`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_groups_rules--client_matcher--client_choice--ip_threat_category_list))

<a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_groups_rules--client_matcher--client_choice--client_selector"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules.api_groups_rules.client_matcher.client_choice.client_selector`

Required:

- `expressions` (List of String) expressions expressions contains the kubernetes style label expression for selections.


<a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_groups_rules--client_matcher--client_choice--ip_threat_category_list"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules.api_groups_rules.client_matcher.client_choice.ip_threat_category_list`

Required:

- `ip_threat_categories` (List of String) IP Threat Categories The IP threat categories is obtained from the list and is used to auto-generate equivalent label selection expressions<br>**Valid Options:** `['BOTNETS', 'DENIAL_OF_SERVICE', 'MOBILE_THREATS', 'NETWORK', 'PHISHING', 'PROXY', 'REPUTATION', 'SCANNERS', 'SPAM_SOURCES', 'TOR_PROXY', 'WEB_ATTACKS', 'WINDOWS_EXPLOITS']` (Multiple selection allowed)



<a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_groups_rules--client_matcher--ip_asn_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules.api_groups_rules.client_matcher.ip_asn_choice`

Optional:

- `any_ip` (Boolean) any ip Any Source IP<br>Conflicts with `asn_list`, `asn_matcher`, `ip_matcher`, and `ip_prefix_list`.
- `asn_list` (Attributes) asn list List of 4-byte ASN values. The predicate evaluates to true if the origin ASN is present in the ASN list.<br>Conflicts with `any_ip`, `asn_matcher`, `ip_matcher`, and `ip_prefix_list`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_groups_rules--client_matcher--ip_asn_choice--asn_list))
- `asn_matcher` (Attributes) asn matcher List of references to BGP ASN Set objects. The predicate evaluates to true if the origin ASN is present in one of the BGP ASN Set objects.<br>Conflicts with `any_ip`, `asn_list`, `ip_matcher`, and `ip_prefix_list`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_groups_rules--client_matcher--ip_asn_choice--asn_matcher))
- `ip_matcher` (Attributes) ip matcher List of references to IP Prefix Set objects. The predicate evaluates to true if the client IP Address is covered by one or more of the IP Prefixes in the IP Prefix Sets.<br>Conflicts with `any_ip`, `asn_list`, `asn_matcher`, and `ip_prefix_list`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_groups_rules--client_matcher--ip_asn_choice--ip_matcher))
- `ip_prefix_list` (Attributes) ip prefix list List of IP Prefixes values. The predicate evaluates to true if the client IP Address is covered by one or more of the IP Prefixes from the list.<br>Conflicts with `any_ip`, `asn_list`, `asn_matcher`, and `ip_matcher`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_groups_rules--client_matcher--ip_asn_choice--ip_prefix_list))

<a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_groups_rules--request_matcher"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules.api_groups_rules.request_matcher`

Optional:

- `cookie_matchers` (Attributes List) cookie matchers A list of predicates for all cookies that need to be matched. The criteria for matching each cookie is described in individual instances of CookieMatcherType. The actual cookie values are extracted from the request API as a list of strings for each cookie name. Note that all specified cookie matcher predicates must evaluate to true. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_groups_rules--request_matcher--cookie_matchers))
- `headers` (Attributes List) headers A list of predicates for various HTTP headers that need to match. The criteria for matching each HTTP header are described in individual HeaderMatcherType instances. The actual HTTP header values are extracted from the request API as a list of strings for each HTTP header type. Note that all specified header predicates must evaluate to true. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_groups_rules--request_matcher--headers))
- `jwt_claims` (Attributes List) JWT claims A list of predicates for various JWT claims that need to match. The criteria for matching each JWT claim are described in individual JWTClaimMatcherType instances. The actual JWT claims values are extracted from the JWT payload as a list of strings. Note that all specified JWT claim predicates must evaluate to true. Note that this feature only works on LBs with JWT Validation feature enabled. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_groups_rules--request_matcher--jwt_claims))
- `query_params` (Attributes List) query params A list of predicates for all query parameters that need to be matched. The criteria for matching each query parameter are described in individual instances of QueryParameterMatcherType. The actual query parameter values are extracted from the request API as a list of strings for each query parameter name. Note that all specified query parameter predicates must evaluate to true. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_groups_rules--request_matcher--query_params))
