Required:

- `key` (String) key A case-sensitive HTTP query parameter name.
- `match_choice` (Attributes) match Select Match Options.<br>Exactly one of `check_not_present`, `check_present`, or `item` must be specified. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_groups_rules--request_matcher--query_params--match_choice))

Optional:

- `invert_matcher` (Boolean) invert_matcher Invert the match result.<br>**Default:** `false`

<a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_groups_rules--request_matcher--query_params--match_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules.api_groups_rules.request_matcher.query_params.match_choice`

Optional:

- `check_not_present` (Boolean) check_not_present Check that the query parameter is not present.<br>Conflicts with `check_present` and `item`.
- `check_present` (Boolean) check_present Check that the query parameter is present.<br>Conflicts with `check_not_present` and `item`.
- `item` (Attributes) item Criteria for matching the values for the given query parameter. The match is successful if any of the values for the query parameter satisfies the criteria in the matcher.<br>Conflicts with `check_not_present` and `check_present`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_groups_rules--request_matcher--query_params--match_choice--item))

<a id="nestedatt--api_protection_rules--api_groups_rules--request_matcher--query_params--match_choice--item"></a>
### Nested Schema for `api_protection_rules.api_groups_rules.request_matcher.query_params.match_choice.item`

Optional:

- `exact_values` (List of String) exact values A list of exact values to match the input against.
- `regex_values` (List of String) regex values A list of regular expressions to match the input against.
- `transformers` (List of String) transformers An ordered list of transformers (starting from index 0) to be applied to the path before matching.<br>**Valid Options:** `['BASE64_DECODE', 'LOWER_CASE', 'NORMALIZE_PATH', 'REMOVE_WHITESPACE', 'TRANSFORMER_NONE', 'TRIM', 'TRIM_LEFT', 'TRIM_RIGHT', 'UPPER_CASE', 'URL_DECODE']` (Multiple selection allowed)







<a id="nestedatt--blocked_clients"></a>
### Nested Schema for `blocked_clients`

Required:

- `actions` (List of String) actions Actions that should be taken when client identifier matches the rule<br>**Valid Options:** `['SKIP_PROCESSING_API_PROTECTION', 'SKIP_PROCESSING_BOT', 'SKIP_PROCESSING_DDOS_PROTECTION', 'SKIP_PROCESSING_IP_REPUTATION', 'SKIP_PROCESSING_MALWARE_PROTECTION', 'SKIP_PROCESSING_MUM', 'SKIP_PROCESSING_OAS_VALIDATION', 'SKIP_PROCESSING_THREAT_MESH', 'SKIP_PROCESSING_WAF']` (Multiple selection allowed)
- `client_source_choice` (Attributes) Client Identifier Client identifier that should be used for the client rule<br>Exactly one of `as_number`, `http_header`, `ip_prefix`, `ipv6_prefix`, or `user_identifier` must be specified. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--blocked_clients--client_source_choice))
- `metadata` (Attributes) metadata Common attributes for the rule including name and description. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--blocked_clients--metadata))

Optional:

- `expiration_timestamp` (String) expiration timestamp The expiration_timestamp is the RFC 3339 format timestamp at which the containing rule is considered to be logically expired. The rule continues to exist in the configuration but is not applied anymore.

<a id="nestedatt--blocked_clients--client_source_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `blocked_clients.client_source_choice`

Optional:

- `as_number` (Number) as number RFC 6793 defined 4-byte AS number<br>Conflicts with `http_header`, `ip_prefix`, `ipv6_prefix`, and `user_identifier`.
- `http_header` (Attributes) HTTP Header Request header name and value pairs<br>Conflicts with `as_number`, `ip_prefix`, `ipv6_prefix`, and `user_identifier`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--blocked_clients--client_source_choice--http_header))
- `ip_prefix` (String) ip prefix IPv4 prefix string.<br>Conflicts with `as_number`, `http_header`, `ipv6_prefix`, and `user_identifier`.
- `ipv6_prefix` (String) ipv6 prefix IPv6 prefix string.<br>Conflicts with `as_number`, `http_header`, `ip_prefix`, and `user_identifier`.
- `user_identifier` (String) user identifier Identify user based on user identifier. User identifier value needs to be copied from security event.<br>**Validation:** `Length LengthAtMost(256)`<br>Conflicts with `as_number`, `http_header`, `ip_prefix`, and `ipv6_prefix`.

<a id="nestedatt--bot_defense_choice--bot_defense--policy"></a>
### Nested Schema for `bot_defense_choice.bot_defense.policy`

Required:

- `java_script_choice` (Attributes) JavaScript Choice This defines a JavaScript insertion rule.<br>Exactly one of `disable_js_insert`, `js_insert_all_pages`, `js_insert_all_pages_except`, or `js_insertion_rules` must be specified. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--bot_defense_choice--bot_defense--policy--java_script_choice))
- `javascript_mode` (List of String) javascript_mode Determine the mode in which the JavaScript is loaded into the entry page. The JavaScript is split into 2 chunks. The larger chunk can be loaded asynchronously or synchronously. It can also be cacheable or non-cacheable on the browser.<br>**Allowed Values (choose one):** `['ASYNC_JS_CACHING', 'ASYNC_JS_NO_CACHING', 'SYNC_JS_CACHING', 'SYNC_JS_NO_CACHING']`
- `protected_app_endpoints` (Attributes List) AppEndpointType List of protected endpoints. Limit: Approx '128 endpoints per Load Balancer (LB)' upto 4 LBs, '32 endpoints per LB' after 4 LBs. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--bot_defense_choice--bot_defense--policy--protected_app_endpoints))

Optional:

- `js_download_path` (String) js_download_path Customize Bot Defense Client JavaScript path. If not specified, default `/common.js`<br>**Default:** `/common.js`
- `mobile_sdk_choice` (Attributes) Mobile SDK Choice This defines mobile SDK configuration.<br>Exactly one of `disable_mobile_sdk` or `mobile_sdk_config` must be specified when `mobile_sdk_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--bot_defense_choice--bot_defense--policy--mobile_sdk_choice))

### Nested Schema for `bot_defense_choice.bot_defense.policy.protected_app_endpoints.mitigation.action_type_choice.block`

Optional:

- `body` (String) body Custom body message is of type uri_ref. Currently supported URL schemes is string:///. For string:/// scheme, message needs to be encoded in Base64 format. You can specify this message as base64 encoded plain text message e.g. 'Your request was blocked' or it can be HTML paragraph or a body string encoded as base64 string E.g. <a id="nestedatt--challenge_type_choice--captcha_challenge"></a>
### Nested Schema for `challenge_type_choice.captcha_challenge`

Optional:

- `cookie_expiry` (Number) cookie_expiry Cookie expiration period, in seconds. An expired cookie causes the loadbalancer to issue a new challenge.<br>**Default:** `3600`
- `custom_page` (String) custom_page Custom message is of type uri_ref. Currently supported URL schemes is string:///. For string:/// scheme, message needs to be encoded in Base64 format. You can specify this message as base64 encoded plain text message e.g. 'Please Wait..' or it can be HTML paragraph or a body string encoded as base64 string E.g. '<p> Please Wait </p>'. Base64 encoded string for this html is 'PHA+IFBsZWFzZSBXYWl0IDwvcD4='<br>**Validation:** `Length LengthAtMost(65536)`

### Nested Schema for `challenge_type_choice.enable_challenge`

(see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--challenge_type_choice--enable_challenge--captcha_challenge_parameters_choice))

- `malicious_user_mitigation_choice` (Attributes) Malicious user mitigation choice Settings that specify the actions to be taken when malicious users are determined to be at different threat levels. User's activity is monitored and continuously analyzed for malicious behavior. From this analysis, a threat-level is assigned to each user. The settings defined in malicious user mitigation specify what mitigation actions to take for user determined to be at different threat levels.<br>Exactly one of `default_mitigation_settings` or `malicious_user_mitigation` must be specified when `malicious_user_mitigation_choice` is configured. - `cookie_expiry` (Number) cookie_expiry Cookie expiration period, in seconds. An expired cookie causes the loadbalancer to issue a new challenge.<br>**Default:** `3600`
- `custom_page` (String) custom_page Custom message is of type uri_ref. Currently supported URL schemes is string:///. For string:/// scheme, message needs to be encoded in Base64 format. You can specify this message as base64 encoded plain text message e.g. 'Please Wait..' or it can be HTML paragraph or a body string encoded as base64 string E.g. '<p> Please Wait </p>'. Base64 encoded string for this html is 'PHA+IFBsZWFzZSBXYWl0IDwvcD4='<br>**Validation:** `Length LengthAtMost(65536)`



<a id="nestedatt--challenge_type_choice--policy_based_challenge--challenge_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `challenge_type_choice.policy_based_challenge.challenge_choice`

Optional:

- `always_enable_captcha_challenge` (Boolean) always enable captcha challenge Enable Captcha challenge for all requests. Challenge rules can be used to selectively disable Captcha challenge or enable JavaScript challenge for some requests.<br>Conflicts with `always_enable_js_challenge` and `no_challenge`.
- `always_enable_js_challenge` (Boolean) always enable JS challenge Enable JavaScript challenge for all requests. Challenge rules can be used to selectively disable JavaScript challenge or enable Captcha challenge for some requests.<br>Conflicts with `always_enable_captcha_challenge` and `no_challenge`.
- `no_challenge` (Boolean) no_challenge Disable JavaScript and Captcha challenge for all requests. Challenge rules can be used to selectively enable JavaScript or Captcha challenge for some requests.<br>Conflicts with `always_enable_captcha_challenge` and `always_enable_js_challenge`.

- `js_challenge_parameters` (Attributes) JavaScript Challenge Configure JavaScript challenge parameters<br>Conflicts with `default_js_challenge_parameters`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--challenge_type_choice--policy_based_challenge--js_challenge_parameters_choice--js_challenge_parameters))

<a id="nestedatt--challenge_type_choice--policy_based_challenge--js_challenge_parameters_choice--js_challenge_parameters"></a>

- `custom_page` (String) custom_page Custom message is of type uri_ref. Currently supported URL schemes is string:///. For string:/// scheme, message needs to be encoded in Base64 format. You can specify this message as base64 encoded plain text message e.g. 'Please Wait..' or it can be HTML paragraph or a body string encoded as base64 string E.g. '<p> Please Wait </p>'. Base64 encoded string for this html is 'PHA+IFBsZWFzZSBXYWl0IDwvcD4='<br>**Validation:** `Length LengthAtMost(65536)`
- `js_script_delay` (Number) js_script_delay Delay introduced by Javascript, in milliseconds.<br>**Default:** `5000`

- `transformers` (List of String) transformers An ordered list of transformers (starting from index 0) to be applied to the path before matching.<br>**Valid Options:** `['BASE64_DECODE', 'LOWER_CASE', 'NORMALIZE_PATH', 'REMOVE_WHITESPACE', 'TRANSFORMER_NONE', 'TRIM', 'TRIM_LEFT', 'TRIM_RIGHT', 'UPPER_CASE', 'URL_DECODE']` (Multiple selection allowed)

Optional:

- `classes` (List of String) classes A list of known classes of TLS fingerprints to match the input TLS JA3 fingerprint against.<br>**Valid Options:** `['ADWARE', 'ADWIND', 'ANY_MALICIOUS_FINGERPRINT', 'DRIDEX', 'GOOTKIT', 'GOZI', 'JBIFROST', 'QUAKBOT', 'RANSOMWARE', 'TOFSEE', 'TORRENTLOCKER', 'TRICKBOT', 'TROLDESH']` (Multiple selection allowed)

- `excluded_values` (List of String) excluded values A list of TLS JA3 fingerprints to be excluded when matching the input TLS JA3 fingerprint. This can be used to skip known false positives when using one or more known TLS fingerprint classes in the enclosing matcher.

<a id="nestedatt--cors_policy"></a>
### Nested Schema for `cors_policy`

Optional:

- `allow_credentials` (Boolean) allow_credentials Specifies whether the resource allows credentials<br>**Default:** `false`
- `allow_headers` (String) allow_headers Specifies the content for the access-control-allow-headers header<br>**Default:** ``
- `allow_methods` (String) allow_methods Specifies the content for the access-control-allow-methods header
- `allow_origin` (List of String) allow_origin Specifies the origins that will be allowed to do CORS requests. An origin is allowed if either allow_origin or allow_origin_regex match
- `allow_origin_regex` (List of String) allow_origin_regex Specifies regex patterns that match allowed origins. An origin is allowed if either allow_origin or allow_origin_regex match
- `disabled` (Boolean) disabled Disable the CorsPolicy for a particular route. This is useful when virtual-host has CorsPolicy, but we need to disable it on a specific route. The value of this field is ignored for virtual-host<br>**Default:** `false`
- `expose_headers` (String) expose_headers Specifies the content for the access-control-expose-headers header<br>**Default:** ``
- `maximum_age` (Number) maximum_age This indicates the maximum number of seconds the results can be cached A value of -1 will disable caching. Maximum permitted value is 86400 seconds (24 hours)<br>**Default:** `0`

- `prefix` (String) prefix Path prefix to match (e.g. the value / will match on all paths)<br>**Validation:** `Length LengthAtMost(256)`<br>Conflicts with `path` and `regex`.
- `regex` (String) regex Regular expression of path match (e.g. the value .* will match on all paths)<br>Conflicts with `path` and `prefix`.

<a id="nestedatt--default_route_pools"></a>
### Nested Schema for `default_route_pools`

Required:

- `pool_choice` (Attributes) Pool Choice Select origin pool method, simple origin pool method or more flexible cluster object.<br>Exactly one of `cluster` or `pool` must be specified. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--default_route_pools--pool_choice))

Optional:

- `endpoint_subsets` (Map of String) Origin Servers Subset Upstream origin pool may be configured to divide its origin servers into subsets based on metadata attached to the origin servers. Routes may then specify the metadata that a endpoint must match in order to be selected by the load balancer For origin servers which are discovered in K8S or Consul cluster, the label of the service is merged with endpoint's labels. In case of Consul, the label is derived from the 'Tag' field. For labels that are common between configured endpoint and discovered service, labels from discovered service takes precedence. List of key-value pairs that will be used as matching metadata. Only those origin servers of upstream origin pool which match this metadata will be selected for load balancing
- `priority` (Number) Priority Priority of this origin pool, valid only with multiple origin pools. Value of 0 will make the pool as lowest priority origin pool Priority of 1 means highest priority and is considered active. When active origin pool is not available, lower priority origin pools are made active as per the increasing priority.<br>**Default:** `1`
- `weight` (Number) Weight Weight of this origin pool, valid only with multiple origin pool. Value of 0 will disable the pool<br>**Default:** `1`

<a id="nestedatt--default_route_pools--pool_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `default_route_pools.pool_choice`

Optional:

- `cluster` (Attributes) Cluster More flexible, advanced feature control with cluster<br>Conflicts with `pool`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--default_route_pools--pool_choice--cluster))
- `pool` (Attributes) Pool Simple, commonly used pool parameters with origin pool<br>Conflicts with `cluster`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--default_route_pools--pool_choice--pool))

<a id="nestedatt--graphql_rules--metadata"></a>

Required:

Optional:

- `description` (String) description Human readable description.<br>**Validation:** `Length LengthAtMost(256)`


<a id="nestedatt--graphql_rules--domain_choice"></a>

(see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--graphql_rules--graphql_settings--allow_introspection_queries_choice))

<a id="nestedatt--hash_policy_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `hash_policy_choice`

Optional:

- `cookie_stickiness` (Attributes) Cookie Based Stickiness Request are sent to all eligible origin servers using hash of cookie. Cookie can be passive(present in the cookies header) or generated(hashing the source and destination ports and addresses). Consistent hashing algorithm, ring hash, is used to select origin server<br>Conflicts with `least_active`, `random`, `ring_hash`, `round_robin`, and `source_ip_stickiness`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--hash_policy_choice--cookie_stickiness))
- `least_active` (Boolean) Least Active Requests Request are sent to origin server that has least active requests<br>Conflicts with `cookie_stickiness`, `random`, `ring_hash`, `round_robin`, and `source_ip_stickiness`.
- `random` (Boolean) Random Request are sent to all eligible origin servers in random fashion<br>Conflicts with `cookie_stickiness`, `least_active`, `ring_hash`, `round_robin`, and `source_ip_stickiness`.
- `ring_hash` (Attributes) Ring Hash Policy Request are sent to all eligible origin servers using hash of request based on hash policy. Consistent hashing algorithm, ring hash, is used to select origin server<br>Conflicts with `cookie_stickiness`, `least_active`, `random`, `round_robin`, and `source_ip_stickiness`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--hash_policy_choice--ring_hash))
- `round_robin` (Boolean) Round Robin Request are sent to all eligible origin servers in round robin fashion<br>Conflicts with `cookie_stickiness`, `least_active`, `random`, `ring_hash`, and `source_ip_stickiness`.
- `source_ip_stickiness` (Boolean) Source IP Stickiness Request are sent to all eligible origin servers using hash of source ip. Consistent hashing algorithm, ring hash, is used to select origin server<br>Conflicts with `cookie_stickiness`, `least_active`, `random`, `ring_hash`, and `round_robin`.

<a id="nestedatt--hash_policy_choice--cookie_stickiness"></a>
### Nested Schema for `hash_policy_choice.cookie_stickiness`

Required:

- `name` (String) name The name of the cookie that will be used to obtain the hash key. If the cookie is not present and TTL below is not set, no hash will be produced<br>**Validation:** `Length LengthBetween(1, 256)`

Optional:

- `httponly_choice` (Attributes) httponly A cookie with the HttpOnly attribute is inaccessible to the JavaScript.<br>Exactly one of `add_httponly` or `ignore_httponly` must be specified when `httponly_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--hash_policy_choice--cookie_stickiness--httponly_choice))
- `path` (String) path The name of the path for the cookie. If no path is specified here, no path will be set for the cookie<br>**Default:** ``
- `samesite_choice` (Attributes) samesite Controls whether or not a cookie is sent with cross-site requests<br>Exactly one of `ignore_samesite`, `samesite_lax`, `samesite_none`, or `samesite_strict` must be specified when `samesite_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--hash_policy_choice--cookie_stickiness--samesite_choice))
- `secure_choice` (Attributes) secure A cookie with the Secure attribute is only sent to the server with an encrypted request over the HTTPS protocol and therefore, is more resistant to man-in-the-middle attacks.<br>Exactly one of `add_secure` or `ignore_secure` must be specified when `secure_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--hash_policy_choice--cookie_stickiness--secure_choice))
- `ttl` (Number) ttl If specified, a cookie with the TTL will be generated if the cookie is not present. If the TTL is present and zero, the generated cookie will be a session cookie. TTL value is in milliseconds<br>**Default:** `0`

<a id="nestedatt--hash_policy_choice--cookie_stickiness--httponly_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `hash_policy_choice.cookie_stickiness.httponly_choice`

Optional:

- `add_httponly` (Boolean) add_httponly Add httponly attribute<br>Conflicts with `ignore_httponly`.
- `ignore_httponly` (Boolean) ignore_httponly Ignore httponly attribute<br>Conflicts with `add_httponly`.


<a id="nestedatt--hash_policy_choice--cookie_stickiness--samesite_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `hash_policy_choice.cookie_stickiness.samesite_choice`

Optional:

- `ignore_samesite` (Boolean) ignore_samesite Ignore Samesite attribute<br>Conflicts with `samesite_lax`, `samesite_none`, and `samesite_strict`.
- `samesite_lax` (Boolean) lax Add Samesite attribute with Lax. Means that the cookie is not sent on cross-site requests<br>Conflicts with `ignore_samesite`, `samesite_none`, and `samesite_strict`.
- `samesite_none` (Boolean) none Add Samesite attribute with None. Means that the browser sends the cookie with both cross-site and same-site requests<br>Conflicts with `ignore_samesite`, `samesite_lax`, and `samesite_strict`.
- `samesite_strict` (Boolean) strict Add Samesite attribute with Strict. Means that the browser sends the cookie only for same-site requests<br>Conflicts with `ignore_samesite`, `samesite_lax`, and `samesite_none`.


<a id="nestedatt--hash_policy_choice--cookie_stickiness--secure_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `hash_policy_choice.cookie_stickiness.secure_choice`

Optional:

- `add_secure` (Boolean) add_secure Add secure attribute<br>Conflicts with `ignore_secure`.
- `ignore_secure` (Boolean) ignore_secure Ignore secure attribute<br>Conflicts with `add_secure`.



<a id="nestedatt--hash_policy_choice--ring_hash"></a>

Each hash policy is evaluated individually and the combined result is used to route the request (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--hash_policy_choice--ring_hash--hash_policy))

(see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--hash_policy_choice--ring_hash--hash_policy--policy_specifier_choice))

Optional:

<a id="nestedatt--hash_policy_choice--ring_hash--hash_policy--policy_specifier_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `hash_policy_choice.ring_hash.hash_policy.policy_specifier_choice`

Optional:

- `header_name` (String) Header The name or key of the request header that will be used to obtain the hash key<br>**Validation:** `Length LengthBetween(1, 256)`<br>Conflicts with `cookie` and `source_ip`.
- `source_ip` (Boolean) Source IP Hash based on source IP address<br>Conflicts with `cookie` and `header_name`.

<a id="nestedatt--hash_policy_choice--ring_hash--hash_policy--policy_specifier_choice--cookie"></a>
### Nested Schema for `hash_policy_choice.ring_hash.hash_policy.policy_specifier_choice.cookie`

Required:

- `name` (String) name The name of the cookie that will be used to obtain the hash key. If the cookie is not present and TTL below is not set, no hash will be produced<br>**Validation:** `Length LengthBetween(1, 256)`

Optional:

- `httponly_choice` (Attributes) httponly A cookie with the HttpOnly attribute is inaccessible to the JavaScript.<br>Exactly one of `add_httponly` or `ignore_httponly` must be specified when `httponly_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--hash_policy_choice--ring_hash--hash_policy--policy_specifier_choice--cookie--httponly_choice))
- `path` (String) path The name of the path for the cookie. If no path is specified here, no path will be set for the cookie
- `samesite_choice` (Attributes) samesite Controls whether or not a cookie is sent with cross-site requests<br>Exactly one of `ignore_samesite`, `samesite_lax`, `samesite_none`, or `samesite_strict` must be specified when `samesite_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--hash_policy_choice--ring_hash--hash_policy--policy_specifier_choice--cookie--samesite_choice))
- `secure_choice` (Attributes) secure A cookie with the Secure attribute is only sent to the server with an encrypted request over the HTTPS protocol and therefore, is more resistant to man-in-the-middle attacks.<br>Exactly one of `add_secure` or `ignore_secure` must be specified when `secure_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--hash_policy_choice--ring_hash--hash_policy--policy_specifier_choice--cookie--secure_choice))
- `ttl` (Number) ttl If specified, a cookie with the TTL will be generated if the cookie is not present. If the TTL is present and zero, the generated cookie will be a session cookie. TTL value is in milliseconds

Optional:

- `ignore_httponly` (Boolean) ignore_httponly Ignore httponly attribute<br>Conflicts with `add_httponly`.


<a id="nestedatt--hash_policy_choice--ring_hash--hash_policy--policy_specifier_choice--cookie--samesite_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `hash_policy_choice.ring_hash.hash_policy.policy_specifier_choice.cookie.samesite_choice`

Optional:

- `ignore_samesite` (Boolean) ignore_samesite Ignore Samesite attribute<br>Conflicts with `samesite_lax`, `samesite_none`, and `samesite_strict`.
- `samesite_lax` (Boolean) lax Add Samesite attribute with Lax. Means that the cookie is not sent on cross-site requests<br>Conflicts with `ignore_samesite`, `samesite_none`, and `samesite_strict`.
- `samesite_none` (Boolean) none Add Samesite attribute with None. Means that the browser sends the cookie with both cross-site and same-site requests<br>Conflicts with `ignore_samesite`, `samesite_lax`, and `samesite_strict`.
- `samesite_strict` (Boolean) strict Add Samesite attribute with Strict. Means that the browser sends the cookie only for same-site requests<br>Conflicts with `ignore_samesite`, `samesite_lax`, and `samesite_none`.

- `ignore_secure` (Boolean) ignore_secure Ignore secure attribute<br>Conflicts with `add_secure`.

### Nested Schema for `jwt_validation.reserved_claims`

Required:

- `audience_validation_choice` (Attributes) audience_validation The value of the aud claim in the JWT token should match one of the configured values<br>Exactly one of `audience` or `audience_disable` must be specified. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--jwt_validation--reserved_claims--audience_validation_choice))

Optional:

- `issuer_validation_choice` (Attributes) issuer_validation Validates the iss claim in JWT tokens. When Local Input is the JWKS source, this global configuration applies. When Authorization Servers are selected, each server's issuer configuration takes precedence, this global configuration is used as a fallback if issuer validation is absent or disabled on the Authorization Server.<br>Exactly one of `issuer` or `issuer_disable` must be specified when `issuer_validation_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--jwt_validation--reserved_claims--issuer_validation_choice))
- `validate_period_choice` (Attributes) validate_period Validate that current time is before the Expiration Time (as specified in the exp claim). If exp claim is not present JWT validation fails. If Not Before (nbf) claim is present in the JWT token validate that current time is after the nbf value.<br>Exactly one of `validate_period_disable` or `validate_period_enable` must be specified when `validate_period_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--jwt_validation--reserved_claims--validate_period_choice))

<a id="nestedatt--l7_ddos_protection"></a>
### Nested Schema for `l7_ddos_protection`

Optional:

- `clientside_action_choice` (Attributes) Client-Side Challenge Configure client-side challenge settings for incoming requests<br>Exactly one of `clientside_action_captcha_challenge`, `clientside_action_js_challenge`, or `clientside_action_none` must be specified when `clientside_action_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--l7_ddos_protection--clientside_action_choice))
- `ddos_policy_choice` (Attributes) Custom Service Policy Select a service policy that will be activated only during an ongoing DDoS attack. This policy will be executed in addition and after internal L7 DDoS Auto Mitigation Rules, but before all other service policies.<br>Exactly one of `ddos_policy_custom` or `ddos_policy_none` must be specified when `ddos_policy_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--l7_ddos_protection--ddos_policy_choice))
- `mitigation_action_choice` (Attributes) Mitigation Action Select a technique to apply on sources which are detected as suspicious by L7 DDoS detection mechanism<br>Exactly one of `mitigation_block`, `mitigation_captcha_challenge`, or `mitigation_js_challenge` must be specified when `mitigation_action_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--l7_ddos_protection--mitigation_action_choice))
- `rps_threshold_choice` (Attributes) RPS Threshold Choice An L7 DDoS attack is identified based on service degradation indicators combined with elevated RPS levels. Configure the RPS threshold that is considered high for the server. By default, this is set to 10,000 RPS.<br>Exactly one of `default_rps_threshold` or `rps_threshold` must be specified when `rps_threshold_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--l7_ddos_protection--rps_threshold_choice))

<a id="nestedatt--l7_ddos_protection--clientside_action_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `l7_ddos_protection.clientside_action_choice`

Optional:

- `clientside_action_captcha_challenge` (Attributes) CAPTCHA Challenge Serve CAPTCHA challenge to all sources<br>Conflicts with `clientside_action_js_challenge` and `clientside_action_none`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--l7_ddos_protection--clientside_action_choice--clientside_action_captcha_challenge))
- `clientside_action_js_challenge` (Attributes) JavaScript Challenge Serve JavaScript challenge to all sources<br>Conflicts with `clientside_action_captcha_challenge` and `clientside_action_none`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--l7_ddos_protection--clientside_action_choice--clientside_action_js_challenge))
- `clientside_action_none` (Boolean) None Don't apply any challenge<br>Conflicts with `clientside_action_captcha_challenge` and `clientside_action_js_challenge`.

<a id="nestedatt--l7_ddos_protection--clientside_action_choice--clientside_action_captcha_challenge"></a>
### Nested Schema for `l7_ddos_protection.clientside_action_choice.clientside_action_captcha_challenge`

Optional:

- `cookie_expiry` (Number) cookie_expiry Cookie expiration period, in seconds. An expired cookie causes the loadbalancer to issue a new challenge.<br>**Default:** `3600`
- `custom_page` (String) custom_page Custom message is of type uri_ref. Currently supported URL schemes is string:///. For string:/// scheme, message needs to be encoded in Base64 format. You can specify this message as base64 encoded plain text message e.g. 'Please Wait..' or it can be HTML paragraph or a body string encoded as base64 string E.g. '<p> Please Wait </p>'. Base64 encoded string for this html is 'PHA+IFBsZWFzZSBXYWl0IDwvcD4='<br>**Validation:** `Length LengthAtMost(65536)`


<a id="nestedatt--l7_ddos_protection--clientside_action_choice--clientside_action_js_challenge"></a>

Optional:

- `cookie_expiry` (Number) cookie_expiry Cookie expiration period, in seconds. An expired cookie causes the loadbalancer to issue a new challenge.<br>**Default:** `3600`

You can specify this message as base64 encoded plain text message e.g. 'Please Wait..' or it can be HTML paragraph or a body string encoded as base64 string E.g. '<p> Please Wait </p>'. Base64 encoded string for this html is 'PHA+IFBsZWFzZSBXYWl0IDwvcD4='<br>**Validation:** `Length LengthAtMost(65536)`
- `js_script_delay` (Number) js_script_delay Delay introduced by Javascript, in milliseconds.<br>**Default:** `5000`

<a id="nestedatt--more_option"></a>
### Nested Schema for `more_option`

Optional:

- `buffer_policy` (Attributes) Buffer configuration for requests Some upstream applications are not capable of handling streamed data and high network latency. This config enables buffering the entire request before sending to upstream application. We can specify the maximum buffer size and buffer interval with this config. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--more_option--buffer_policy))
- `compression_params` (Attributes) Compression configuration Enables load balancer to compress dispatched data from an upstream service upon client request. Only GZIP compression is supported (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--more_option--compression_params))
- `custom_errors` (Map of String) Custom Errors Map of integer error codes as keys and string values that can be used to provide custom http pages for each error code. Key of the map can be either response code class or HTTP Error code. Response code classes for key is configured as follows 3 -- for 3xx response code class 4 -- for 4xx response code class 5 -- for 5xx response code class Value of the map is string which represents custom HTTP responses. Specific response code takes preference when both response code and response code class matches for a request.
- `disable_default_error_pages` (Boolean) Disable the use of default F5XC error pages Disable the use of default F5XC error pages.<br>**Default:** `false`
- `http10_choice` (Attributes) Allow HTTP/1.0 Control whether HTTP/1.0 and HTTP/0.9 requests are accepted or rejected on this load balancer.<br>Exactly one of `disable_http10` or `enable_http10` must be specified when `http10_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--more_option--http10_choice))
- `idle_timeout` (Number) Idle timeout The amount of time that a stream can exist without upstream or downstream activity, in milliseconds. The stream is terminated with a HTTP 504 (Gateway Timeout) error code if no upstream response header has been received, otherwise the stream is reset.<br>**Default:** `30000`
- `max_request_header_size` (Number) Maximum request header size The maximum request header size for downstream connections, in KiB. A HTTP 431 (Request Header Fields Too Large) error code is sent for requests that exceed this size. If multiple load balancers share the same advertise_policy, the highest value configured across all such load balancers is used for all the load balancers in question.<br>**Default:** `60`
- `max_requests_per_connection_choice` (Attributes) max_requests_per_connection Sets the maximum number of requests a downstream client can send over a single connection to Envoy.<br>Exactly one of `max_requests_per_connection` or `no_request_limit_per_connection` must be specified when `max_requests_per_connection_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--more_option--max_requests_per_connection_choice))
- `request_cookies_to_add` (Attributes List) Cookies to add in request Cookies are key-value pairs to be added to HTTP request being routed towards upstream. Cookies specified at this level are applied after cookies from matched Route are applied (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--more_option--request_cookies_to_add))
- `request_cookies_to_remove` (List of String) Cookies to be removed from request List of keys of Cookies to be removed from the HTTP request being sent towards upstream.
- `request_headers_to_add` (Attributes List) Headers to add in request Headers are key-value pairs to be added to HTTP request being routed towards upstream. Headers specified at this level are applied after headers from matched Route are applied (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--more_option--request_headers_to_add))
- `request_headers_to_remove` (List of String) Header to be removed from request List of keys of Headers to be removed from the HTTP request being sent towards upstream.
- `response_cookies_to_add` (Attributes List) Cookies to add in set-cookie header in response Cookies are name-value pairs along with optional attribute parameters to be added to HTTP response being sent towards downstream. Cookies specified at this level are applied after cookies from matched Route are applied (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--more_option--response_cookies_to_add))
- `response_cookies_to_remove` (List of String) Cookies to be removed from response List of name of Cookies to be removed from the HTTP response being sent towards downstream. Entire set-cookie header will be removed
- `response_headers_to_add` (Attributes List) Headers to add in response Headers are key-value pairs to be added to HTTP response being sent towards downstream. Headers specified at this level are applied after headers from matched Route are applied (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--more_option--response_headers_to_add))
- `response_headers_to_remove` (List of String) Header to be removed from response List of keys of Headers to be removed from the HTTP response being sent towards downstream.

<a id="nestedatt--more_option--buffer_policy"></a>
### Nested Schema for `more_option.buffer_policy`

Optional:

- `disabled` (Boolean) disable Disable buffering for a particular route. This is useful when virtual-host has buffering, but we need to disable it on a specific route. The value of this field is ignored for virtual-host<br>**Default:** `false`
- `max_request_bytes` (Number) max_request_bytes The maximum request size that the filter will buffer before the connection manager will stop buffering and return a RequestEntityTooLarge (413) response.


<a id="nestedatt--more_option--compression_params"></a>
### Nested Schema for `more_option.compression_params`

Optional:

- `content_length` (Number) content_length Minimum response length, in bytes, which will trigger compression. The default value is 30.
- `content_type` (List of String) content_type Set of strings that allows specifying which mime-types yield compression When this field is not defined, compression will be applied to the following mime-types: 'application/javascript' 'application/json', 'application/xhtml+xml' 'image/svg+xml' 'text/css' 'text/html' 'text/plain' 'text/xml'
- `disable_on_etag_header` (Boolean) disable_on_etag_header If true, disables compression when the response contains an etag header. When it is false, weak etags will be preserved and the ones that require strong validation will be removed.<br>**Default:** `false`
- `remove_accept_encoding_header` (Boolean) remove_accept_encoding_header If true, removes accept-encoding from the request headers before dispatching it to the upstream so that responses do not get compressed before reaching the filter.<br>**Default:** `false`


<a id="nestedatt--more_option--http10_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `more_option.http10_choice`

Optional:

- `disable_http10` (Boolean) Disable HTTP/1.0 Reject HTTP/1.0 and HTTP/0.9 traffic on this LB.<br>Conflicts with `enable_http10`.
- `enable_http10` (Boolean) Enable HTTP/1.0 Allow HTTP/1.0 and HTTP/0.9 traffic on this LB.<br>Conflicts with `disable_http10`.


<a id="nestedatt--more_option--max_requests_per_connection_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `more_option.max_requests_per_connection_choice`

Optional:

- `max_requests_per_connection` (Number) Maximum Requests Per Connection Sets the maximum number of requests a downstream client can send over a single connection to Envoy. Enter a value >=1 to define the request limit per connection.<br>Conflicts with `no_request_limit_per_connection`.
- `no_request_limit_per_connection` (Boolean) Disable the max requests per connection option This option disables the maximum requests per connection limit. When selected, no limit is enforced, and connections can handle unlimited requests.<br>Conflicts with `max_requests_per_connection`.

(see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--more_option--response_cookies_to_add--partitioned_choice))

(see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--more_option--response_cookies_to_add--value_choice--secret_value--secret_info_choice--blindfold_secret_info))
- `clear_secret_info` (Attributes) Clear Secret Clear Secret is used for the secrets that are not encrypted<br>Conflicts with `blindfold_secret_info` and `none`. <a id="nestedatt--origin_server_subset_rule_list"></a>
### Nested Schema for `origin_server_subset_rule_list`

Optional:

- `origin_server_subset_rules` (Attributes List) Origin Server Subset Origin Server Subset Rules allow users to define match condition on Client (IP address, ASN, Country), IP Reputation, Regional Edge names, Request for subset selection of origin servers. Origin Server Subset  is a sequential engine where rules are evaluated one after the other. It's important to define the correct order for Origin Server Subset  to get the intended result, rules are evaluated from top to bottom in the list. When an Origin server subset rule is matched, then this selection rule takes effect and no more rules are evaluated. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--origin_server_subset_rule_list--origin_server_subset_rules))

Note: The pre-requisite settings to be configured in the origin pool are: 1. Add labels to origin servers 2. The predicate evaluates to true if the origin ASN is present in one of the BGP ASN Set objects.<br>Conflicts with `any_asn` and `asn_list`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--origin_server_subset_rule_list--origin_server_subset_rules--asn_choice--asn_matcher))

<a id="nestedatt--origin_server_subset_rule_list--origin_server_subset_rules--selector_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `origin_server_subset_rule_list.origin_server_subset_rules.selector_choice`

Optional:

- `client_selector` (Attributes) client selector A label selector that describes the expected set of clients. The labels associated with the client making the API request are used to evaluate the label expressions in the selector. These labels can be derived from the client TLS certificate or from the volterra internal control plane. This is a more flexible and powerful version of the client name matcher predicate that allows a given rule to be applicable to a set of clients based on the client labels rather than being limited to relying on patterns in the client name. The predicate evaluates to true if the expressions in the label selector are true for the client labels.<br>Conflicts with `none`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--origin_server_subset_rule_list--origin_server_subset_rules--selector_choice--client_selector))
- `none` (Boolean) No Label Selector No Label Selector<br>Conflicts with `client_selector`.

<a id="nestedatt--origin_server_subset_rule_list--origin_server_subset_rules--selector_choice--client_selector"></a>
### Nested Schema for `origin_server_subset_rule_list.origin_server_subset_rules.selector_choice.client_selector`

Required:

- `expressions` (List of String) expressions expressions contains the kubernetes style label expression for selections.





<a id="nestedatt--protected_cookies"></a>
### Nested Schema for `protected_cookies`

Required:

- `name` (String) name Name of the Cookie<br>**Validation:** `Length LengthAtMost(256)`

Optional:

- `cookie_tampering_choice` (Attributes) cookie_tampering Cookie Tampering Protection prevents attackers from modifying the value of session cookies. To use this feature, Web Application Firewall must be enabled.<br>Exactly one of `disable_tampering_protection` or `enable_tampering_protection` must be specified when `cookie_tampering_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--protected_cookies--cookie_tampering_choice))
- `httponly_choice` (Attributes) httponly A cookie with the HttpOnly attribute is inaccessible to the JavaScript.<br>Exactly one of `add_httponly` or `ignore_httponly` must be specified when `httponly_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--protected_cookies--httponly_choice))
- `samesite_choice` (Attributes) samesite Controls whether or not a cookie is sent with cross-site requests<br>Exactly one of `ignore_samesite`, `samesite_lax`, `samesite_none`, or `samesite_strict` must be specified when `samesite_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--protected_cookies--samesite_choice))
- `secure_choice` (Attributes) secure A cookie with the Secure attribute is only sent to the server with an encrypted request over the HTTPS protocol and therefore, is more resistant to man-in-the-middle attacks.<br>Exactly one of `add_secure` or `ignore_secure` must be specified when `secure_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--protected_cookies--secure_choice))

<a id="nestedatt--protected_cookies--cookie_tampering_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `protected_cookies.cookie_tampering_choice`

Optional:

- `disable_tampering_protection` (Boolean) disable<br>Conflicts with `enable_tampering_protection`.
- `enable_tampering_protection` (Boolean) enable<br>Conflicts with `disable_tampering_protection`.


<a id="nestedatt--protected_cookies--httponly_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `protected_cookies.httponly_choice`

Optional:

- `add_httponly` (Boolean) add_httponly<br>Conflicts with `ignore_httponly`.
- `ignore_httponly` (Boolean) ignore_httponly<br>Conflicts with `add_httponly`.


<a id="nestedatt--protected_cookies--samesite_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `protected_cookies.samesite_choice`

Optional:

- `ignore_samesite` (Boolean) ignore_samesite Ignore Samesite attribute<br>Conflicts with `samesite_lax`, `samesite_none`, and `samesite_strict`.
- `samesite_lax` (Boolean) lax Add Samesite attribute with Lax. Means that the cookie is not sent on cross-site requests<br>Conflicts with `ignore_samesite`, `samesite_none`, and `samesite_strict`.
- `samesite_none` (Boolean) none Add Samesite attribute with None. Means that the browser sends the cookie with both cross-site and same-site requests<br>Conflicts with `ignore_samesite`, `samesite_lax`, and `samesite_strict`.
- `samesite_strict` (Boolean) strict Add Samesite attribute with Strict. Means that the browser sends the cookie only for same-site requests<br>Conflicts with `ignore_samesite`, `samesite_lax`, and `samesite_none`.


<a id="nestedatt--protected_cookies--secure_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `protected_cookies.secure_choice`

Optional:

- `add_secure` (Boolean) add_secure<br>Conflicts with `ignore_secure`.
- `ignore_secure` (Boolean) ignore_secure<br>Conflicts with `add_secure`.

For creating rule that contain a whole domain or group of endpoints, please use the server URL rules above. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules))
- `ip_allowed_list_choice` (Attributes) IP Allowed List Allowed List of IPs for which rate limiting will be disabled.<br>Exactly one of `bypass_rate_limiting_rules`, `custom_ip_allowed_list`, `ip_allowed_list`, or `no_ip_allowed_list` must be specified when `ip_allowed_list_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--ip_allowed_list_choice))
- `server_url_rules` (Attributes List) server_url_policy Set of rules for entire domain or base path that contain multiple endpoints. Order is matter as it uses first match policy. For matching also specific endpoints you can use the API endpoint rules set bellow. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--server_url_rules))

<a id="nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rate_limit_choice.api_rate_limit.api_endpoint_rules`

Required:

- `api_endpoint_path` (String) api endpoint path The endpoint (path) of the request.<br>**Validation:** `Length LengthAtMost(1024)`
- `rate_limiter_choice` (Attributes) Rate limit values This defines the values of the rate limiter.<br>Exactly one of `inline_rate_limiter` or `ref_rate_limiter` must be specified. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--rate_limiter_choice))

Optional:

- `api_endpoint_method` (Attributes) method The list of expected values for the HTTP method in the request API. The actual value of the HTTP method is extracted from the HTTP request. The predicate evaluates to true if the actual HTTP method belongs is present in the list of expected values. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--api_endpoint_method))
- `client_matcher` (Attributes) client_matcher Conditions related to the origin of the request, such as client IP, TLS fingerprint, etc. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher))
- `domain_choice` (Attributes) domain choices Choose if the rule will apply for all domains or a specific one.<br>Exactly one of `any_domain` or `specific_domain` must be specified when `domain_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--domain_choice))
- `request_matcher` (Attributes) request_matcher Conditions related to the request, such as query parameters, headers, etc. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--request_matcher))

<a id="nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--rate_limiter_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rate_limit_choice.api_rate_limit.api_endpoint_rules.rate_limiter_choice`

Optional:

- `inline_rate_limiter` (Attributes) Inline Rate Limiter Specify rate values for the rule.<br>Conflicts with `ref_rate_limiter`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--rate_limiter_choice--inline_rate_limiter))
- `ref_rate_limiter` (Attributes) External Rate Limiter Select external rate limiter.<br>Conflicts with `inline_rate_limiter`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--rate_limiter_choice--ref_rate_limiter))

<a id="nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--rate_limiter_choice--inline_rate_limiter"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rate_limit_choice.api_rate_limit.api_endpoint_rules.rate_limiter_choice.inline_rate_limiter`

Required:

- `unit` (List of String) rate Unit for the period per which the rate limit is applied.<br>**Allowed Values (choose one):** `['DAY', 'HOUR', 'MINUTE', 'SECOND']`

Optional:

- `count_by_choice` (Attributes) Count by The classification criteria for requests counts.<br>Exactly one of `ref_user_id` or `use_http_lb_user_id` must be specified when `count_by_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--rate_limiter_choice--inline_rate_limiter--count_by_choice))
- `threshold` (Number) threshold The total number of allowed requests for 1 unit (e.g. SECOND/MINUTE/HOUR etc.) of the specified period.<br>**Default:** `1`

<a id="nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--rate_limiter_choice--inline_rate_limiter--count_by_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rate_limit_choice.api_rate_limit.api_endpoint_rules.rate_limiter_choice.inline_rate_limiter.count_by_choice`

Optional:

- `ref_user_id` (Attributes) ref_user_id A reference to user_identification object. The rules in the user_identification object are evaluated to determine the user identifier to be rate limited. If traffic cannot be identified by the rules in the user_identification object, by default it will be identified by the HTTP-LB User Identifier.<br>Conflicts with `use_http_lb_user_id`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--rate_limiter_choice--inline_rate_limiter--count_by_choice--ref_user_id))
- `use_http_lb_user_id` (Boolean) use_http_lb_user_id Defined in HTTP-LB Security Configuration -> User Identifier.<br>Conflicts with `ref_user_id`.

<a id="nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--rate_limiter_choice--inline_rate_limiter--count_by_choice--ref_user_id"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rate_limit_choice.api_rate_limit.api_endpoint_rules.rate_limiter_choice.inline_rate_limiter.count_by_choice.ref_user_id`

Required:

- `name` (String)
- `namespace` (String)

Optional:

- `tenant` (String)




<a id="nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--rate_limiter_choice--ref_rate_limiter"></a>

Required:

- `name` (String)
- `namespace` (String)

Optional:

- `tenant` (String)



<a id="nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--api_endpoint_method"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rate_limit_choice.api_rate_limit.api_endpoint_rules.api_endpoint_method`

Optional:

- `invert_matcher` (Boolean) invert_matcher Invert the match result.<br>**Default:** `false`
- `methods` (List of String) methods List of methods values to match against.<br>**Valid Options:** `['ANY', 'CONNECT', 'COPY', 'DELETE', 'GET', 'HEAD', 'OPTIONS', 'PATCH', 'POST', 'PUT', 'TRACE']` (Multiple selection allowed)


<a id="nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rate_limit_choice.api_rate_limit.api_endpoint_rules.client_matcher`

Optional:

- `client_choice` (Attributes) client choice Select clients for which the rule will be applied. The actual names of the client are extracted from its TLS certificate.<br>Exactly one of `any_client`, `client_selector`, or `ip_threat_category_list` must be specified when `client_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--client_choice))
- `ip_asn_choice` (Attributes) ip asn choice Match source IP address/ASN  of the request<br>Exactly one of `any_ip`, `asn_list`, `asn_matcher`, `ip_matcher`, or `ip_prefix_list` must be specified when `ip_asn_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--ip_asn_choice))
- `tls_fingerprint_matcher` (Attributes) TLS JA3 fingerprint matcher TLS JA3 fingerprints to be matched. The predicate evaluates to true if the TLS fingerprint matches any of the exact values or classes of known TLS fingerprints. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--tls_fingerprint_matcher))

<a id="nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--client_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rate_limit_choice.api_rate_limit.api_endpoint_rules.client_matcher.client_choice`

Optional:

- `any_client` (Boolean) any ip Any Client<br>Conflicts with `client_selector` and `ip_threat_category_list`.
- `client_selector` (Attributes) client selector A label selector that describes the expected set of clients. The labels associated with the client making the API request are used to evaluate the label expressions in the selector. These labels can be derived from the client TLS certificate or from the volterra internal control plane. This is a more flexible and powerful version of the client name matcher predicate that allows a given rule to be applicable to a set of clients based on the client labels rather than being limited to relying on patterns in the client name. The predicate evaluates to true if the expressions in the label selector are true for the client labels.<br>Conflicts with `any_client` and `ip_threat_category_list`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--client_choice--client_selector))
- `ip_threat_category_list` (Attributes) IP Threat Category List IP threat categories to choose from<br>Conflicts with `any_client` and `client_selector`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--client_choice--ip_threat_category_list))

<a id="nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--client_choice--client_selector"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rate_limit_choice.api_rate_limit.api_endpoint_rules.client_matcher.client_choice.client_selector`

Required:

- `expressions` (List of String) expressions expressions contains the kubernetes style label expression for selections.


<a id="nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--client_choice--ip_threat_category_list"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rate_limit_choice.api_rate_limit.api_endpoint_rules.client_matcher.client_choice.ip_threat_category_list`

Required:

- `ip_threat_categories` (List of String) IP Threat Categories The IP threat categories is obtained from the list and is used to auto-generate equivalent label selection expressions<br>**Valid Options:** `['BOTNETS', 'DENIAL_OF_SERVICE', 'MOBILE_THREATS', 'NETWORK', 'PHISHING', 'PROXY', 'REPUTATION', 'SCANNERS', 'SPAM_SOURCES', 'TOR_PROXY', 'WEB_ATTACKS', 'WINDOWS_EXPLOITS']` (Multiple selection allowed)



<a id="nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--ip_asn_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rate_limit_choice.api_rate_limit.api_endpoint_rules.client_matcher.ip_asn_choice`

Optional:

- `any_ip` (Boolean) any ip Any Source IP<br>Conflicts with `asn_list`, `asn_matcher`, `ip_matcher`, and `ip_prefix_list`.
- `asn_list` (Attributes) asn list List of 4-byte ASN values. The predicate evaluates to true if the origin ASN is present in the ASN list.<br>Conflicts with `any_ip`, `asn_matcher`, `ip_matcher`, and `ip_prefix_list`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--ip_asn_choice--asn_list))
- `asn_matcher` (Attributes) asn matcher List of references to BGP ASN Set objects. The predicate evaluates to true if the origin ASN is present in one of the BGP ASN Set objects.<br>Conflicts with `any_ip`, `asn_list`, `ip_matcher`, and `ip_prefix_list`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--ip_asn_choice--asn_matcher))
- `ip_matcher` (Attributes) ip matcher List of references to IP Prefix Set objects. The predicate evaluates to true if the client IP Address is covered by one or more of the IP Prefixes in the IP Prefix Sets.<br>Conflicts with `any_ip`, `asn_list`, `asn_matcher`, and `ip_prefix_list`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--ip_asn_choice--ip_matcher))
- `ip_prefix_list` (Attributes) ip prefix list List of IP Prefixes values. The predicate evaluates to true if the client IP Address is covered by one or more of the IP Prefixes from the list.<br>Conflicts with `any_ip`, `asn_list`, `asn_matcher`, and `ip_matcher`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--ip_asn_choice--ip_prefix_list))

<a id="nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--ip_asn_choice--asn_list"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rate_limit_choice.api_rate_limit.api_endpoint_rules.client_matcher.ip_asn_choice.asn_list`

Required:

- `as_numbers` (List of Number) as numbers An unordered set of RFC 6793 defined 4-byte AS numbers that can be used to create allow or deny lists for use in network policy or service policy. It can be used to create the allow list only for DNS Load Balancer.


<a id="nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--ip_asn_choice--asn_matcher"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rate_limit_choice.api_rate_limit.api_endpoint_rules.client_matcher.ip_asn_choice.asn_matcher`

Required:

- `namespace` (String)

Optional:

- `tenant` (String)

Required:

Optional:

- `invert_matcher` (Boolean) invert_matcher Invert the match result.<br>**Default:** `false`

Optional:

### Nested Schema for `rate_limit_choice.api_rate_limit.api_endpoint_rules.client_matcher.ip_asn_choice.ip_prefix_list`

Optional:

- `ip_prefixes` (List of String) ip prefixes List of IPv4 prefix strings.
- `ipv6_prefixes` (List of String) ipv6 prefixes List of IPv6 prefix strings.



<a id="nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--client_matcher--tls_fingerprint_matcher"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rate_limit_choice.api_rate_limit.api_endpoint_rules.client_matcher.tls_fingerprint_matcher`

Optional:

- `classes` (List of String) classes A list of known classes of TLS fingerprints to match the input TLS JA3 fingerprint against.<br>**Valid Options:** `['ADWARE', 'ADWIND', 'ANY_MALICIOUS_FINGERPRINT', 'DRIDEX', 'GOOTKIT', 'GOZI', 'JBIFROST', 'QUAKBOT', 'RANSOMWARE', 'TOFSEE', 'TORRENTLOCKER', 'TRICKBOT', 'TROLDESH']` (Multiple selection allowed)
- `exact_values` (List of String) exact values A list of exact TLS JA3 fingerprints to match the input TLS JA3 fingerprint against.
- `excluded_values` (List of String) excluded values A list of TLS JA3 fingerprints to be excluded when matching the input TLS JA3 fingerprint. This can be used to skip known false positives when using one or more known TLS fingerprint classes in the enclosing matcher.



<a id="nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--domain_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rate_limit_choice.api_rate_limit.api_endpoint_rules.domain_choice`

Optional:

- `any_domain` (Boolean) any domain The rule will apply for all domains.<br>Conflicts with `specific_domain`.
- `specific_domain` (String) domain The rule will apply for a specific domain.<br>**Validation:** `Length LengthAtMost(128)`<br>Conflicts with `any_domain`.


<a id="nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--request_matcher"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rate_limit_choice.api_rate_limit.api_endpoint_rules.request_matcher`

Optional:

- `cookie_matchers` (Attributes List) cookie matchers A list of predicates for all cookies that need to be matched. The criteria for matching each cookie is described in individual instances of CookieMatcherType. The actual cookie values are extracted from the request API as a list of strings for each cookie name. Note that all specified cookie matcher predicates must evaluate to true. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--request_matcher--cookie_matchers))
- `headers` (Attributes List) headers A list of predicates for various HTTP headers that need to match. The criteria for matching each HTTP header are described in individual HeaderMatcherType instances. The actual HTTP header values are extracted from the request API as a list of strings for each HTTP header type. Note that all specified header predicates must evaluate to true. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--request_matcher--headers))
- `jwt_claims` (Attributes List) JWT claims A list of predicates for various JWT claims that need to match. The criteria for matching each JWT claim are described in individual JWTClaimMatcherType instances. The actual JWT claims values are extracted from the JWT payload as a list of strings. Note that all specified JWT claim predicates must evaluate to true. Note that this feature only works on LBs with JWT Validation feature enabled. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--request_matcher--jwt_claims))
- `query_params` (Attributes List) query params A list of predicates for all query parameters that need to be matched. The criteria for matching each query parameter are described in individual instances of QueryParameterMatcherType. The actual query parameter values are extracted from the request API as a list of strings for each query parameter name. Note that all specified query parameter predicates must evaluate to true. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--request_matcher--query_params))

<a id="nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--request_matcher--cookie_matchers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rate_limit_choice.api_rate_limit.api_endpoint_rules.request_matcher.cookie_matchers`

Required:

- `match_choice` (Attributes) match Select Match Options.<br>Exactly one of `check_not_present`, `check_present`, or `item` must be specified. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--request_matcher--cookie_matchers--match_choice))
- `name` (String) name A case-sensitive cookie name.

Optional:

- `invert_matcher` (Boolean) invert_matcher Invert Match of the expression defined<br>**Default:** `false`

<a id="nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--request_matcher--cookie_matchers--match_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rate_limit_choice.api_rate_limit.api_endpoint_rules.request_matcher.cookie_matchers.match_choice`

Optional:

- `check_not_present` (Boolean) check_not_present Check that the cookie is not present.<br>Conflicts with `check_present` and `item`.
- `check_present` (Boolean) check_present Check that the cookie is present.<br>Conflicts with `check_not_present` and `item`.
- `item` (Attributes) item Criteria for matching the values for the cookie. The match is successful if any of the values in the input satisfies the criteria in the matcher.<br>Conflicts with `check_not_present` and `check_present`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--request_matcher--cookie_matchers--match_choice--item))

Optional:

- `exact_values` (List of String) exact values A list of exact values to match the input against.
- `regex_values` (List of String) regex values A list of regular expressions to match the input against.
- `transformers` (List of String) transformers An ordered list of transformers (starting from index 0) to be applied to the path before matching.<br>**Valid Options:** `['BASE64_DECODE', 'LOWER_CASE', 'NORMALIZE_PATH', 'REMOVE_WHITESPACE', 'TRANSFORMER_NONE', 'TRIM', 'TRIM_LEFT', 'TRIM_RIGHT', 'UPPER_CASE', 'URL_DECODE']` (Multiple selection allowed)

Required:

- `match_choice` (Attributes) match Select Match Options.<br>Exactly one of `check_not_present`, `check_present`, or `item` must be specified. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--api_endpoint_rules--request_matcher--headers--match_choice))

Optional:

Optional:

- `any_client` (Boolean) any ip Any Client<br>Conflicts with `client_selector` and `ip_threat_category_list`.
- `client_selector` (Attributes) client selector A label selector that describes the expected set of clients. The labels associated with the client making the API request are used to evaluate the label expressions in the selector. These labels can be derived from the client TLS certificate or from the volterra internal control plane. This is a more flexible and powerful version of the client name matcher predicate that allows a given rule to be applicable to a set of clients based on the client labels rather than being limited to relying on patterns in the client name. The predicate evaluates to true if the expressions in the label selector are true for the client labels.<br>Conflicts with `any_client` and `ip_threat_category_list`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--server_url_rules--client_matcher--client_choice--client_selector))

- `cookie_matchers` (Attributes List) cookie matchers A list of predicates for all cookies that need to be matched. The criteria for matching each cookie is described in individual instances of CookieMatcherType. The actual cookie values are extracted from the request API as a list of strings for each cookie name. Note that all specified cookie matcher predicates must evaluate to true. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--server_url_rules--request_matcher--cookie_matchers))
- `headers` (Attributes List) headers A list of predicates for various HTTP headers that need to match. The criteria for matching each HTTP header are described in individual HeaderMatcherType instances. The actual HTTP header values are extracted from the request API as a list of strings for each HTTP header type. Note that all specified header predicates must evaluate to true. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--server_url_rules--request_matcher--headers))
- `jwt_claims` (Attributes List) JWT claims A list of predicates for various JWT claims that need to match. The criteria for matching each JWT claim are described in individual JWTClaimMatcherType instances. The actual JWT claims values are extracted from the JWT payload as a list of strings. Note that all specified JWT claim predicates must evaluate to true. Note that this feature only works on LBs with JWT Validation feature enabled. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--server_url_rules--request_matcher--jwt_claims))
- `query_params` (Attributes List) query params A list of predicates for all query parameters that need to be matched. The criteria for matching each query parameter are described in individual instances of QueryParameterMatcherType. The actual query parameter values are extracted from the request API as a list of strings for each query parameter name. Note that all specified query parameter predicates must evaluate to true. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rate_limit_choice--api_rate_limit--server_url_rules--request_matcher--query_params))

(see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--host_rewrite_params_choice))

<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--origin_pools"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.origin_pools`

Required:

- `pool_choice` (Attributes) Pool Choice Select origin pool method, simple origin pool method or more flexible cluster object.<br>Exactly one of `cluster` or `pool` must be specified. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--origin_pools--pool_choice))

Optional:

- `endpoint_subsets` (Map of String) Origin Servers Subset Upstream origin pool may be configured to divide its origin servers into subsets based on metadata attached to the origin servers. Routes may then specify the metadata that a endpoint must match in order to be selected by the load balancer For origin servers which are discovered in K8S or Consul cluster, the label of the service is merged with endpoint's labels. In case of Consul, the label is derived from the 'Tag' field. For labels that are common between configured endpoint and discovered service, labels from discovered service takes precedence. List of key-value pairs that will be used as matching metadata. Only those origin servers of upstream origin pool which match this metadata will be selected for load balancing
- `priority` (Number) Priority Priority of this origin pool, valid only with multiple origin pools. Value of 0 will make the pool as lowest priority origin pool Priority of 1 means highest priority and is considered active. When active origin pool is not available, lower priority origin pools are made active as per the increasing priority.<br>**Default:** `1`
- `weight` (Number) Weight Weight of this origin pool, valid only with multiple origin pool. Value of 0 will disable the pool<br>**Default:** `1`

- `pool` (Attributes) Pool Simple, commonly used pool parameters with origin pool<br>Conflicts with `cluster`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--origin_pools--pool_choice--pool))
