<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.advanced_options`

Optional:

- `bot_defense_javascript_injection_choice` (Attributes) Oneof Bot Defense JavaScript Injection Specifies whether bot defense javascript injection has a specific configuration for this route<br>Exactly one of `bot_defense_javascript_injection` or `inherited_bot_defense_javascript_injection` must be specified when `bot_defense_javascript_injection_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--bot_defense_javascript_injection_choice))
- `buffer_choice` (Attributes) Enable Route Specific Buffering Enable or disable route specific buffering<br>Exactly one of `buffer_policy` or `common_buffering` must be specified when `buffer_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--buffer_choice))
- `cluster_retract_choice` (Attributes) Oneof for Cluster retraction Specifies whether retraction of cluster has to be enabled or disabled<br>Exactly one of `do_not_retract_cluster` or `retract_cluster` must be specified when `cluster_retract_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--cluster_retract_choice))
- `cors_policy` (Attributes) cors_policy Cross-Origin Resource Sharing requests configuration CORS is a mechanism that uses additional HTTP headers to tell a browser to let a web application running at one origin (domain) have permission to access selected resources from a server at a different origin (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--cors_policy))
- `csrf_policy` (Attributes) csrf_policy Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) is an attack that occurs when a malicious third-party website exploits a vulnerability thats allows them to submit an undesired request on user's behalf. The policy checks where a request is coming from to determine if the request's origin is the same as its destination. The policy relies on two pieces of information used in determining if a request originated from the same host. 1. The origin that caused the user agent to issue the request (source origin). 2. The origin that the request is going to (target origin). When the policy evaluating a request, it ensures both pieces of information are present and compare their values. If the source origin is missing or origins do not match the request is rejected. The exception to this being the source-origin has been added to the policy as valid. Because CSRF attacks specifically target state-changing requests, the policy only acts on the HTTP requests that have state-changing method (PUT,POST, etc.). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--csrf_policy))
- `disable_location_add` (Boolean) disable_location_add virtual-host level. This configuration is ignored on CE sites.<br>**Default:** `false`
- `endpoint_subsets` (Map of String) Origin Servers Subset Upstream origin pool may be configured to divide its origin servers into subsets based on metadata attached to the origin servers. Routes may then specify the metadata that a endpoint must match in order to be selected by the load balancer For origin servers which are discovered in K8S or Consul cluster, the label of the service is merged with endpoint's labels. In case of Consul, the label is derived from the 'Tag' field. For labels that are common between configured endpoint and discovered service, labels from discovered service takes precedence. List of key-value pairs that will be used as matching metadata. Only those origin servers of upstream origin pool which match this metadata will be selected for load balancing
- `hash_policy_choice` (Attributes) Hash Policy Choice Enable route specific hash policy for this route<br>Exactly one of `common_hash_policy` or `specific_hash_policy` must be specified when `hash_policy_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--hash_policy_choice))
- `mirroring_choice` (Attributes) Mirroring Enable/disable Mirroring<br>Exactly one of `disable_mirroring` or `mirror_policy` must be specified when `mirroring_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--mirroring_choice))
- `priority` (List of String) priority Priority routing for each route. Different connection pools are used based on the priority of the route. Also, circuit-breaker configuration at destination cluster is chosen based on the route priority.<br>**Allowed Values (choose one):** `['DEFAULT', 'HIGH']`<br>**Default:** `DEFAULT`
- `request_cookies_to_add` (Attributes List) Cookies to add in request Cookies are key-value pairs to be added to HTTP request being routed towards upstream. Cookies specified at this level are applied after cookies from matched Route are applied (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--request_cookies_to_add))
- `request_cookies_to_remove` (List of String) Cookies to be removed from request List of keys of Cookies to be removed from the HTTP request being sent towards upstream.
- `request_headers_to_add` (Attributes List) Headers to add in request Headers are key-value pairs to be added to HTTP request being routed towards upstream. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--request_headers_to_add))
- `request_headers_to_remove` (List of String) Header to be removed from request List of keys of Headers to be removed from the HTTP request being sent towards upstream.
- `response_cookies_to_add` (Attributes List) Cookies to add in set-cookie header in response Cookies are name-value pairs along with optional attribute parameters to be added to HTTP response being sent towards downstream. Cookies specified at this level are applied after cookies from matched Route are applied (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--response_cookies_to_add))
- `response_cookies_to_remove` (List of String) Cookies to be removed from response List of name of Cookies to be removed from the HTTP response being sent towards downstream. Entire set-cookie header will be removed
- `response_headers_to_add` (Attributes List) Headers to add in response Headers are key-value pairs to be added to HTTP response being sent towards downstream. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--response_headers_to_add))
- `response_headers_to_remove` (List of String) Header to be removed from response List of keys of Headers to be removed from the HTTP response being sent towards downstream.
- `retry_policy_choice` (Attributes) Retry Policy Choice Select default retry policy or configure custom<br>Exactly one of `default_retry_policy`, `no_retry_policy`, or `retry_policy` must be specified when `retry_policy_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--retry_policy_choice))
- `rewrite_choice` (Attributes) Enable Rewrite Select to enable prefix or regex rewrite or disable all options<br>Exactly one of `disable_prefix_rewrite`, `prefix_rewrite`, or `regex_rewrite` must be specified when `rewrite_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--rewrite_choice))
- `spdy_choice` (Attributes) SPDY Choice Select to enable or disable spdy upgrade<br>Exactly one of `disable_spdy` or `enable_spdy` must be specified when `spdy_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--spdy_choice))
- `timeout` (Number) timeout The timeout for the route including all retries, in milliseconds. Should be set to a high value or 0 (infinite timeout) for server-side streaming.<br>**Default:** `30000`
- `waf_choice` (Attributes) Enable the WAF (Web Application Firewall) functionality for VirtualHost WAF can be used to analyze inbound and outbound http/https traffic. WAF can be configured either in BLOCKing Mode or ALERTing Mode. In BLOCKing mode if WAF detects suspicious inbound/outbound traffic it blocks the request or response. In ALERTing mode if suspicious traffic is detected, WAF generates ALERTs with details on the suspicious traffic (instead of blocking traffic).<br>Exactly one of `app_firewall`, `disable_waf`, or `inherited_waf` must be specified when `waf_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--waf_choice))
- `waf_exclusion_choice` (Attributes) Enable the WAF Exclusion functionality for VirtualHost A WAF Exclusion that can be applied to one or more Load Balancers or Routes. The WAF Exclusion is evaluated sequentially and can only be matched once per request.<br>Exactly one of `inherited_waf_exclusion` or `waf_exclusion_policy` must be specified when `waf_exclusion_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--waf_exclusion_choice))
- `websocket_choice` (Attributes) Websocket Choice Select to enable or disable websocket upgrade<br>Exactly one of `disable_web_socket_config` or `web_socket_config` must be specified when `websocket_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--websocket_choice))

<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--buffer_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.advanced_options.buffer_choice`

Optional:

- `buffer_policy` (Attributes) Route Specific Buffering Configuration Buffering configuration for requests Some upstream applications are not capable of handling streamed data. This config enables buffering the entire request before sending to upstream application. We can specify the maximum buffer size and buffer interval with this config. Route level buffer configuration overrides any configuration at VirtualHost level.<br>Conflicts with `common_buffering`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--buffer_choice--buffer_policy))
- `common_buffering` (Boolean) Common buffering Configuration Use common buffering configuration<br>Conflicts with `buffer_policy`.

<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--buffer_choice--buffer_policy"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.advanced_options.buffer_choice.buffer_policy`

Optional:

- `disabled` (Boolean) disable Disable buffering for a particular route. This is useful when virtual-host has buffering, but we need to disable it on a specific route. The value of this field is ignored for virtual-host<br>**Default:** `false`
- `max_request_bytes` (Number) max_request_bytes The maximum request size that the filter will buffer before the connection manager will stop buffering and return a RequestEntityTooLarge (413) response.



<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--cluster_retract_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.advanced_options.cluster_retract_choice`

Optional:

- `do_not_retract_cluster` (Boolean) do_not_retract_cluster When this option is configured, cluster with no healthy endpoints is not retracted from route having weighted cluster configuration.<br>Conflicts with `retract_cluster`.
- `retract_cluster` (Boolean) retract_cluster When this option is enabled, weighted cluster will not be considered for load balancing, if all its endpoints are unhealthy. Since the cluster with all unhealthy endpoints is removed, the traffic will be distributed among remaining clusters as per their weight. Also panic-threshold configuration is ignored for retracted cluster. This option is ignored when single destination cluster is configured for route<br>Conflicts with `do_not_retract_cluster`.


<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--cors_policy"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.advanced_options.cors_policy`

Optional:

- `allow_credentials` (Boolean) allow_credentials Specifies whether the resource allows credentials<br>**Default:** `false`
- `allow_headers` (String) allow_headers Specifies the content for the access-control-allow-headers header
- `allow_methods` (String) allow_methods Specifies the content for the access-control-allow-methods header
- `allow_origin` (List of String) allow_origin Specifies the origins that will be allowed to do CORS requests. An origin is allowed if either allow_origin or allow_origin_regex match
- `allow_origin_regex` (List of String) allow_origin_regex Specifies regex patterns that match allowed origins. An origin is allowed if either allow_origin or allow_origin_regex match
- `disabled` (Boolean) disabled Disable the CorsPolicy for a particular route. This is useful when virtual-host has CorsPolicy, but we need to disable it on a specific route. The value of this field is ignored for virtual-host<br>**Default:** `false`
- `expose_headers` (String) expose_headers Specifies the content for the access-control-expose-headers header
- `maximum_age` (Number) maximum_age This indicates the maximum number of seconds the results can be cached A value of -1 will disable caching. Maximum permitted value is 86400 seconds (24 hours)


<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--csrf_policy"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.advanced_options.csrf_policy`

Optional:

- `allowed_domains_choice` (Attributes) allowed_domains The list of source origin that should be allowed.<br>Exactly one of `all_load_balancer_domains`, `custom_domain_list`, or `disabled` must be specified when `allowed_domains_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--csrf_policy--allowed_domains_choice))

<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--csrf_policy--allowed_domains_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.advanced_options.csrf_policy.allowed_domains_choice`

Optional:

- `all_load_balancer_domains` (Boolean) all_load_balancer_domains Add All load balancer domains to source origin (allow) list.<br>Conflicts with `custom_domain_list` and `disabled`.
- `custom_domain_list` (Attributes) custom_domain_list Add one or more domains to source origin (allow) list.<br>Conflicts with `all_load_balancer_domains` and `disabled`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--csrf_policy--allowed_domains_choice--custom_domain_list))
- `disabled` (Boolean) disabled Allow all source origin domains.<br>Conflicts with `all_load_balancer_domains` and `custom_domain_list`.

<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--csrf_policy--allowed_domains_choice--custom_domain_list"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.advanced_options.csrf_policy.allowed_domains_choice.custom_domain_list`

Required:

- `domains` (List of String) Domains A list of domain names that will be matched to loadbalancer. These domains are not used for SNI match. Wildcard names are supported in the suffix or prefix form.




<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--hash_policy_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.advanced_options.hash_policy_choice`

Optional:

- `common_hash_policy` (Boolean) Common Hash Policy Use load balancer hash policy for this route<br>Conflicts with `specific_hash_policy`.
- `specific_hash_policy` (Attributes) Route Specific Hash Policy Configure hash policy specific for this route<br>Conflicts with `common_hash_policy`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--hash_policy_choice--specific_hash_policy))

<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--hash_policy_choice--specific_hash_policy"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.advanced_options.hash_policy_choice.specific_hash_policy`

Required:

- `hash_policy` (Attributes List) hash_policy Specifies a list of hash policies to use for ring hash load balancing. Each hash policy is evaluated individually and the combined result is used to route the request (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--hash_policy_choice--specific_hash_policy--hash_policy))

<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--hash_policy_choice--specific_hash_policy--hash_policy"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.advanced_options.hash_policy_choice.specific_hash_policy.hash_policy`

Required:

- `policy_specifier_choice` (Attributes) PolicySpecifier Specifies whether hashing is done on incoming request header, cookie or source IP<br>Exactly one of `cookie`, `header_name`, or `source_ip` must be specified. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--hash_policy_choice--specific_hash_policy--hash_policy--policy_specifier_choice))

Optional:

- `terminal` (Boolean) terminal Specify if its a terminal policy<br>**Default:** `false`

<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--hash_policy_choice--specific_hash_policy--hash_policy--policy_specifier_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.advanced_options.hash_policy_choice.specific_hash_policy.hash_policy.policy_specifier_choice`

Optional:

- `cookie` (Attributes) Cookie Hash based on cookie<br>Conflicts with `header_name` and `source_ip`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--hash_policy_choice--specific_hash_policy--hash_policy--policy_specifier_choice--cookie))
- `header_name` (String) Header The name or key of the request header that will be used to obtain the hash key<br>**Validation:** `Length LengthBetween(1, 256)`<br>Conflicts with `cookie` and `source_ip`.
- `source_ip` (Boolean) Source IP Hash based on source IP address<br>Conflicts with `cookie` and `header_name`.

<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--hash_policy_choice--specific_hash_policy--hash_policy--policy_specifier_choice--cookie"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.advanced_options.hash_policy_choice.specific_hash_policy.hash_policy.policy_specifier_choice.cookie`

Required:

- `name` (String) name The name of the cookie that will be used to obtain the hash key. If the cookie is not present and TTL below is not set, no hash will be produced<br>**Validation:** `Length LengthBetween(1, 256)`

Optional:

- `httponly_choice` (Attributes) httponly A cookie with the HttpOnly attribute is inaccessible to the JavaScript.<br>Exactly one of `add_httponly` or `ignore_httponly` must be specified when `httponly_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--hash_policy_choice--specific_hash_policy--hash_policy--policy_specifier_choice--cookie--httponly_choice))
- `path` (String) path The name of the path for the cookie. If no path is specified here, no path will be set for the cookie
- `samesite_choice` (Attributes) samesite Controls whether or not a cookie is sent with cross-site requests<br>Exactly one of `ignore_samesite`, `samesite_lax`, `samesite_none`, or `samesite_strict` must be specified when `samesite_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--hash_policy_choice--specific_hash_policy--hash_policy--policy_specifier_choice--cookie--samesite_choice))
- `secure_choice` (Attributes) secure A cookie with the Secure attribute is only sent to the server with an encrypted request over the HTTPS protocol and therefore, is more resistant to man-in-the-middle attacks.<br>Exactly one of `add_secure` or `ignore_secure` must be specified when `secure_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--hash_policy_choice--specific_hash_policy--hash_policy--policy_specifier_choice--cookie--secure_choice))
- `ttl` (Number) ttl If specified, a cookie with the TTL will be generated if the cookie is not present. If the TTL is present and zero, the generated cookie will be a session cookie. TTL value is in milliseconds

<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--hash_policy_choice--specific_hash_policy--hash_policy--policy_specifier_choice--cookie--httponly_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.advanced_options.hash_policy_choice.specific_hash_policy.hash_policy.policy_specifier_choice.cookie.httponly_choice`

Optional:

- `add_httponly` (Boolean) add_httponly Add httponly attribute<br>Conflicts with `ignore_httponly`.
- `ignore_httponly` (Boolean) ignore_httponly Ignore httponly attribute<br>Conflicts with `add_httponly`.


<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--hash_policy_choice--specific_hash_policy--hash_policy--policy_specifier_choice--cookie--samesite_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.advanced_options.hash_policy_choice.specific_hash_policy.hash_policy.policy_specifier_choice.cookie.samesite_choice`

Optional:

- `ignore_samesite` (Boolean) ignore_samesite Ignore Samesite attribute<br>Conflicts with `samesite_lax`, `samesite_none`, and `samesite_strict`.
- `samesite_lax` (Boolean) lax Add Samesite attribute with Lax. Means that the cookie is not sent on cross-site requests<br>Conflicts with `ignore_samesite`, `samesite_none`, and `samesite_strict`.
- `samesite_none` (Boolean) none Add Samesite attribute with None. Means that the browser sends the cookie with both cross-site and same-site requests<br>Conflicts with `ignore_samesite`, `samesite_lax`, and `samesite_strict`.
- `samesite_strict` (Boolean) strict Add Samesite attribute with Strict. Means that the browser sends the cookie only for same-site requests<br>Conflicts with `ignore_samesite`, `samesite_lax`, and `samesite_none`.


<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--hash_policy_choice--specific_hash_policy--hash_policy--policy_specifier_choice--cookie--secure_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.advanced_options.hash_policy_choice.specific_hash_policy.hash_policy.policy_specifier_choice.cookie.secure_choice`

Optional:

- `add_secure` (Boolean) add_secure Add secure attribute<br>Conflicts with `ignore_secure`.
- `ignore_secure` (Boolean) ignore_secure Ignore secure attribute<br>Conflicts with `add_secure`.







<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--mirroring_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.advanced_options.mirroring_choice`

Optional:

- `disable_mirroring` (Boolean) Disable Mirroring Disable Mirroring of request<br>Conflicts with `mirror_policy`.
- `mirror_policy` (Attributes) Enable Mirroring MirrorPolicy is used for shadowing traffic from one cluster to another. The current implementation is 'fire and forget,' meaning it will not wait for the shadow cluster to respond before returning the response from the primary cluster. All normal statistics are collected for the shadow cluster making this feature useful for testing. During shadowing, the host/authority header is altered such that *-shadow* is appended. This is useful for logging. For example, *cluster1* becomes *cluster1-shadow*.<br>Conflicts with `disable_mirroring`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--mirroring_choice--mirror_policy))

<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--mirroring_choice--mirror_policy"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.advanced_options.mirroring_choice.mirror_policy`

Required:

- `origin_pool` (Attributes) cluster Specifies the cluster to which the requests will be mirrored. The cluster object referred here must be present. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--mirroring_choice--mirror_policy--origin_pool))
- `percent` (Attributes) percent Percentage of requests to be mirrored (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--mirroring_choice--mirror_policy--percent))

<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--mirroring_choice--mirror_policy--origin_pool"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.advanced_options.mirroring_choice.mirror_policy.origin_pool`

Required:

- `name` (String)
- `namespace` (String)

Optional:

- `tenant` (String)


<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--mirroring_choice--mirror_policy--percent"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.advanced_options.mirroring_choice.mirror_policy.percent`

Required:

- `denominator` (List of String) denominator Samples per denominator. numerator part per 100 or 10000 ro 1000000<br>**Allowed Values (choose one):** `['HUNDRED', 'MILLION', 'TEN_THOUSAND']`

Optional:

- `numerator` (Number) numerator sampled parts per denominator. If denominator was 10000, then value of 5 will be 5 in 10000<br>**Default:** `5`




<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--request_cookies_to_add"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.advanced_options.request_cookies_to_add`

Required:

- `name` (String) name Name of the cookie in Cookie header.<br>**Validation:** `Length LengthAtMost(256)`
- `value_choice` (Attributes) value Enter Cookie value as string or blindfolded secret.<br>Exactly one of `secret_value` or `value` must be specified. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--request_cookies_to_add--value_choice))

Optional:

### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.advanced_options.request_cookies_to_add.value_choice`

Optional:

- `secret_value` (Attributes) Secret Value Secret Value of the Cookie header<br>Conflicts with `value`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--request_cookies_to_add--value_choice--secret_value))
- `value` (String) value Value of the Cookie header.<br>**Validation:** `Length LengthAtMost(8096)`<br>Conflicts with `secret_value`.

<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--request_cookies_to_add--value_choice--secret_value"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.advanced_options.request_cookies_to_add.value_choice.secret_value`

Required:

- `secret_info_choice` (Attributes) SecretInfoOneof Secret can be one of the following types - * Blindfold Secret - Secret is managed by F5XC Secret Management System * Clear Secret - Secret is not encrypted<br>Exactly one of `blindfold_secret_info`, `clear_secret_info`, or `none` must be specified. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--request_cookies_to_add--value_choice--secret_value--secret_info_choice))

<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--request_cookies_to_add--value_choice--secret_value--secret_info_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.advanced_options.request_cookies_to_add.value_choice.secret_value.secret_info_choice`

Optional:

- `blindfold_secret_info` (Attributes) Blindfold Secret Blindfold Secret is used for the secrets managed by F5XC Secret Management Service<br>Conflicts with `clear_secret_info` and `none`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--request_cookies_to_add--value_choice--secret_value--secret_info_choice--blindfold_secret_info))
- `clear_secret_info` (Attributes) Clear Secret Clear Secret is used for the secrets that are not encrypted<br>Conflicts with `blindfold_secret_info` and `none`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--request_cookies_to_add--value_choice--secret_value--secret_info_choice--clear_secret_info))
- `none` (Boolean) None No private key will be stored or used. Choose this only when you need a public certificate for verification (e.g., validating SAML/JWT signatures). Not suitable for TLS or any use case that requires presenting a certificate, those will fail without a private key.<br>Conflicts with `blindfold_secret_info` and `clear_secret_info`.

<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--request_cookies_to_add--value_choice--secret_value--secret_info_choice--blindfold_secret_info"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.advanced_options.request_cookies_to_add.value_choice.secret_value.secret_info_choice.blindfold_secret_info`

Required:

Optional:

- `decryption_provider` (String) Decryption Provider Name of the Secret Management Access object that contains information about the backend Secret Management service.
- `store_provider` (String) Store Provider Name of the Secret Management Access object that contains information about the store to get encrypted bytes This field needs to be provided only if the url scheme is not string:///


<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--request_cookies_to_add--value_choice--secret_value--secret_info_choice--clear_secret_info"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.advanced_options.request_cookies_to_add.value_choice.secret_value.secret_info_choice.clear_secret_info`

Required:

- `url` (String, Sensitive) URL URL of the secret. Currently supported URL schemes is string:///. For string:/// scheme, Secret needs to be encoded Base64 format. When asked for this secret, caller will get Secret bytes after Base64 decoding.

Optional:

- `provider` (String) Provider Name of the Secret Management Access object that contains information about the store to get encrypted bytes This field needs to be provided only if the url scheme is not string:///

- `samesite_strict` (Boolean) strict Add Samesite attribute with Strict. Means that the browser sends the cookie only for same-site requests<br>Conflicts with `ignore_samesite`, `samesite_lax`, and `samesite_none`.

(see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--response_cookies_to_add--value_choice--secret_value--secret_info_choice--blindfold_secret_info))

Not suitable for TLS or any use case that requires presenting a certificate, those will fail without a private key.<br>Conflicts with `blindfold_secret_info` and `clear_secret_info`.

<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--response_cookies_to_add--value_choice--secret_value--secret_info_choice--blindfold_secret_info"></a>

Optional:

- `decryption_provider` (String) Decryption Provider Name of the Secret Management Access object that contains information about the backend Secret Management service.
- `store_provider` (String) Store Provider Name of the Secret Management Access object that contains information about the store to get encrypted bytes This field needs to be provided only if the url scheme is not string:///


<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--response_cookies_to_add--value_choice--secret_value--secret_info_choice--clear_secret_info"></a>

Optional:

- `provider` (String) Provider Name of the Secret Management Access object that contains information about the store to get encrypted bytes This field needs to be provided only if the url scheme is not string:///

<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--retry_policy_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.advanced_options.retry_policy_choice`

Optional:

- `default_retry_policy` (Boolean) Use Default Retry Policy Use system default retry policy<br>Conflicts with `no_retry_policy` and `retry_policy`.
- `no_retry_policy` (Boolean) No retry policy Do not configure retry policy<br>Conflicts with `default_retry_policy` and `retry_policy`.
- `retry_policy` (Attributes) Custom Retry Policy Configure custom retry policy<br>Conflicts with `default_retry_policy` and `no_retry_policy`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--retry_policy_choice--retry_policy))

<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--retry_policy_choice--retry_policy"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.advanced_options.retry_policy_choice.retry_policy`

Required:

- `retry_condition` (List of String) retry_condition Specifies the conditions under which retry takes place. Retries can be on different types of condition depending on application requirements. For example, network failure, all 5xx response codes, idempotent 4xx response codes, etc The possible values are '5xx'             : Retry will be done if the upstream server responds with any 5xx response code, or does not respond at all (disconnect/reset/read timeout). 'gateway-error'   : Retry will be done only if the upstream server responds with 502, 503 or 504 responses (Included in 5xx) 'connect-failure' : Retry will be done if the request fails because of a connection failure to the upstream server (connect timeout, etc.). (Included in 5xx) 'refused-stream'  : Retry is done if the upstream server resets the stream with a REFUSED_STREAM error code (Included in 5xx) 'retriable-4xx'   : Retry is done if the upstream server responds with a retriable 4xx response code. The only response code in this category is HTTP CONFLICT (409) 'retriable-status-codes' :  Retry is done if the upstream server responds with any response code matching one defined in retriable_status_codes field 'reset'           : Retry is done if the upstream server does not respond at all (disconnect/reset/read timeout.)<br>**Valid Options:** `['5xx', 'gateway-error', 'connect-failure', 'refused-stream', 'retriable-4xx', 'retriable-status-codes', 'reset']` (Multiple selection allowed)

Optional:

- `back_off` (Attributes) Retry BackOff Specifies parameters that control retry back off. This parameter is optional, in which case the default base interval is 25 milliseconds. The default maximum interval is 10 times the base interval (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--retry_policy_choice--retry_policy--back_off))
- `num_retries` (Number) num_retries Specifies the allowed number of retries. Defaults to 1. Retries can be done any number of times. An exponential back-off algorithm is used between each retry<br>**Default:** `1`
- `per_try_timeout` (Number) per_try_timeout Specifies a non-zero timeout per retry attempt. In milliseconds
- `retriable_status_codes` (List of Number) Retriable status Code HTTP status codes that should trigger a retry in addition to those specified by retry_on.

<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--retry_policy_choice--retry_policy--back_off"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.advanced_options.retry_policy_choice.retry_policy.back_off`

Optional:

- `base_interval` (Number) base_interval Specifies the base interval between retries in milliseconds<br>**Default:** `25`
- `max_interval` (Number) max_interval Specifies the maximum interval between retries in milliseconds. This parameter is optional, but must be greater than or equal to the base_interval if set. The default is 10 times the base_interval.




<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--rewrite_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.advanced_options.rewrite_choice`

Optional:

- `disable_prefix_rewrite` (Boolean) Disable Rewrite Do not rewrite any path portion.<br>Conflicts with `prefix_rewrite` and `regex_rewrite`.
- `prefix_rewrite` (String) prefix_rewrite prefix_rewrite indicates that during forwarding, the matched prefix (or path) should be swapped with its value. When using regex path matching, the entire path (not including the query string) will be swapped with this value.<br>**Validation:** `Length LengthAtMost(256)`<br>Conflicts with `disable_prefix_rewrite` and `regex_rewrite`.
- `regex_rewrite` (Attributes) regex_rewrite regex_rewrite indicates that during forwarding, the matched regex should be swapped with the substitution value.<br>Conflicts with `disable_prefix_rewrite` and `prefix_rewrite`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--rewrite_choice--regex_rewrite))

<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--rewrite_choice--regex_rewrite"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.advanced_options.rewrite_choice.regex_rewrite`

Optional:

- `pattern` (String) Pattern The regular expression used to find portions of a string that should be replaced.<br>**Validation:** `Length LengthBetween(1, 256)`
- `substitution` (String) Substitution The string that should be substituted into matching portions of the subject string during a substitution operation to produce a new string.<br>**Validation:** `Length LengthAtMost(256)`

<a id="nestedatt--routes--choice--simple_route--advanced_options--waf_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `routes.choice.simple_route.advanced_options.waf_choice`

- `disable_waf` (Boolean) disable_app_firewall App Firewall configuration that is configured in the Load Balancer will not be enforced on this route<br>Conflicts with `app_firewall` and `inherited_waf`.
- `inherited_waf` (Boolean) Inherited WAF App Firewall configuration is taken from the Load Balancer. Hence no custom configuration is applied on the route<br>Conflicts with `app_firewall` and `disable_waf`.

- `no_service_policies` (Boolean) Do Not Apply Service Policies Do not apply any service policies i.e. bypass the namespace service policy set<br>Conflicts with `active_service_policies` and `service_policies_from_namespace`.
- `service_policies_from_namespace` (Boolean) Apply Namespace Service Policies Apply the active service policies configured as part of the namespace service policy set<br>Conflicts with `active_service_policies` and `no_service_policies`.

<a id="nestedatt--service_policy_choice--active_service_policies"></a>
### Nested Schema for `service_policy_choice.active_service_policies`

Required:

- `policies` (Attributes List) policies Service Policies is a sequential engine where policies (and rules within the policy) are evaluated one after the other. It's important to define the correct order (policies evaluated from top to bottom in the list) for service policies, to get the intended result. For each request, its characteristics are evaluated based on the match criteria in each service policy starting at the top. If there is a match in the current policy, then the policy takes effect, and no more policies are evaluated. Otherwise, the next policy is evaluated. If all policies are evaluated and none match, then the request will be denied by default. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--service_policy_choice--active_service_policies--policies))

- `namespace` (String)

- `tenant` (String)

<a id="nestedatt--slow_ddos_mitigation_choice--slow_ddos_mitigation"></a>
### Nested Schema for `slow_ddos_mitigation_choice.slow_ddos_mitigation`

Required:

- `request_timeout_choice` (Attributes) Total Request Timeout The amount of time allowed for the entire request stream to be received from the client, in milliseconds. The stream is terminated with a HTTP 408 (Request Timeout) error code if request has not been completed. The default value is 60000 milliseconds. This setting provides protection against Slow POST attacks.<br>Exactly one of `disable_request_timeout` or `request_timeout` must be specified. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--slow_ddos_mitigation_choice--slow_ddos_mitigation--request_timeout_choice))

Optional:

- `request_headers_timeout` (Number) Request Headers Timeout The amount of time the client has to send only the headers on the request stream before the stream is cancelled. The default value is 10000 milliseconds. This setting provides protection against Slowloris attacks.<br>**Default:** `10000`

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).


<a id="nestedatt--trust_client_ip_headers_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `trust_client_ip_headers_choice`

Optional:

- `disable_trust_client_ip_headers` (Boolean) Disable<br>Conflicts with `enable_trust_client_ip_headers`.
- `enable_trust_client_ip_headers` (Attributes) Enable<br>Conflicts with `disable_trust_client_ip_headers`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--trust_client_ip_headers_choice--enable_trust_client_ip_headers))

<a id="nestedatt--trust_client_ip_headers_choice--enable_trust_client_ip_headers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `trust_client_ip_headers_choice.enable_trust_client_ip_headers`

Required:

- `client_ip_headers` (List of String) Client IP Headers Specify one or more HTTP header names that can contain the client IP address. The system evaluates the headers in the configured order and uses the first header that is present in the request. If multiple configured headers are present, the configured order determines which header takes precedence. If the request contains multiple instances of the selected header, the system concatenates their values in the order they appear (comma-separated) before evaluating them. For headers other than X-Forwarded-For, the system uses the rightmost IP address when the header contains multiple IP addresses. For X-Forwarded-For, the system skips IP addresses from the right according to the 'Trusted Proxy Hops for X-Forwarded-For setting' and uses the next IP address as the client IP. If none of the configured headers are present, if the selected value is not a valid IP address, or if the X-Forwarded-For header contains fewer IPs than the configured trusted hops, the system uses the source IP address of the incoming connection. Configure only headers that are inserted or overwritten by trusted proxies.

Optional:

- `xff_num_trusted_hops_choice` (Attributes) Trusted Proxy Hops for X-Forwarded-For Specify how many IP addresses to skip from the right in the X-Forwarded-For header. A value of 1 skips the rightmost IP address, 2 skips the two rightmost IP addresses, and so on. This setting applies only when X-Forwarded-For is included in the Client IP Headers list.<br>Exactly one of `xff_num_trusted_hops_custom` or `xff_num_trusted_hops_default` must be specified when `xff_num_trusted_hops_choice` is configured. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--trust_client_ip_headers_choice--enable_trust_client_ip_headers--xff_num_trusted_hops_choice))

<a id="nestedatt--trust_client_ip_headers_choice--enable_trust_client_ip_headers--xff_num_trusted_hops_choice"></a>
### Nested Schema for `trust_client_ip_headers_choice.enable_trust_client_ip_headers.xff_num_trusted_hops_choice`

Optional:

- `xff_num_trusted_hops_custom` (Number) Custom Trusted Hops Specify the number of IP addresses to skip from the right in the X-Forwarded-For header before selecting the client IP address. The minimum value is 1.<br>Conflicts with `xff_num_trusted_hops_default`.
- `xff_num_trusted_hops_default` (Boolean) Default Trusted Hops Use one trusted proxy hop. The system skips the rightmost IP address in the X-Forwarded-For header.<br>Conflicts with `xff_num_trusted_hops_custom`.

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an `import` block to import this resource by ID.

> **Note:** Replace placeholder values (for example, `<namespace>`, `<name>`) with actual values.

#### Command-Line Import

Use the following `command` to import this resource from the command line:

```shell
terraform import f5xc_http_loadbalancer.example <namespace>/<name>
```

#### HCL Import Block

Use the following `hcl` block to import this resource during `plan` or `apply`:

```hcl
import {
	id = "<namespace>/<name>"
	to = f5xc_http_loadbalancer.example
}
```
